1: //! GTK-native design-token defaults + color-scheme detection (spec/TOKENS.md).
2: //!
3: //! The renderer owns default token values and the effective color scheme.
4: //! Tier-1 defaults start as **concrete platform-appropriate fallbacks**
5: //! ([`concrete_default_tables`]); when a real widget exists, the tokens the
6: //! current GTK theme can resolve are replaced with **native colors** via
7: //! `gtk::StyleContext::lookup_color` of the theme's named colors (`@theme_*`,
8: //! `@borders`, `@success_color`, …). Headless / theme-missing → pure concrete
9: //! fallback, which keeps tests deterministic.
10: 
11: use std::collections::BTreeMap;
12: 
13: use gtk::prelude::*;
14: use pathland_core::tokens::{Scheme, TokenValue};
15: 
16: use crate::host::concrete_default_tables;
17: 
18: /// GTK theme named color → canonical Tier-1 token path. A resolver that returns
19: /// `None` for a name keeps the concrete fallback for that token.
20: const NAMED_COLORS: &[(&str, &str)] = &[
21:     ("theme_bg_color", "color.background"),
22:     ("theme_base_color", "color.surface"),
23:     ("theme_fg_color", "color.text.primary"),
24:     ("theme_unfocused_fg_color", "color.text.secondary"),
25:     ("theme_selected_bg_color", "color.accent"),
26:     ("theme_selected_bg_color", "color.primary"),
27:     ("theme_selected_fg_color", "color.text.onPrimary"),
28:     ("borders", "color.border"),
29:     ("success_color", "color.success"),
30:     ("warning_color", "color.warning"),
31:     ("error_color", "color.danger"),
32: ];
33: 
34: /// Derive the effective scheme from a `GtkSettings` object.
35: #[allow(deprecated)] // gtk_application_prefer_dark_theme is deprecated; the 4.14 `gtk-color-scheme` isn't in this binding
36: pub fn scheme_from_settings(settings: &gtk::Settings) -> Scheme {
37:     let dark = settings.is_gtk_application_prefer_dark_theme()
38:         || settings
39:             .gtk_theme_name()
40:             .as_deref()
41:             .map_or(false, |name| name.ends_with("-dark"));
42:     if dark {
43:         Scheme::Dark
44:     } else {
45:         Scheme::Light
46:     }
47: }
48: 
49: /// Build the Tier-1 default tables (light + dark), replacing the tokens the
50: /// `resolve` closure can map (a widget's style-context theme lookup) with
51: /// native colors **for the given scheme**. GTK exposes one theme at a time, so
52: /// only the *active* scheme's defaults are native; the other scheme keeps its
53: /// concrete fallback.
54: pub fn enrich_defaults<F>(
55:     resolve: &F,
56:     scheme: Scheme,
57: ) -> (BTreeMap<String, TokenValue>, BTreeMap<String, TokenValue>)
58: where
59:     F: Fn(&str) -> Option<u32>,
60: {
61:     let (mut base, mut dark) = concrete_default_tables();
62:     let target = match scheme {
63:         Scheme::Dark => &mut dark,
64:         Scheme::Light => &mut base,
65:     };
66:     for (name, path) in NAMED_COLORS {
67:         if let Some(argb) = resolve(name) {
68:             target.insert((*path).to_string(), TokenValue::Color(argb));
69:         }
70:     }
71:     (base, dark)
72: }
73: 
74: /// Resolve a GTK theme named color (`@theme_*`, `@borders`, …) to
75: /// `0xAARRGGBB` via a style context, or `None` when the theme doesn't define it.
76: pub fn lookup_color(ctx: &gtk::StyleContext, name: &str) -> Option<u32> {
77:     ctx.lookup_color(name).map(|rgba| {
78:         let a = (rgba.alpha() * 255.0).round().clamp(0.0, 255.0) as u32;
79:         let r = (rgba.red() * 255.0).round() as u32;
80:         let g = (rgba.green() * 255.0).round() as u32;
81:         let b = (rgba.blue() * 255.0).round() as u32;
82:         (a << 24) | (r << 16) | (g << 8) | b
83:     })
84: }
85:

87: mod tests {
88:     use super::*;
89: 
90:     #[test]
91:     fn named_color_mapping_covers_core_tokens() {
92:         let paths: Vec<&str> = NAMED_COLORS.iter().map(|(_, p)| *p).collect();
93:         for core in [
94:             "color.background",
95:             "color.surface",
96:             "color.text.primary",
97:             "color.accent",
98:             "color.primary",
99:             "color.border",
100:             "color.success",

103:         ] {

105:         }

115:         );

122:     }

124:     #[test]
125:     fn enrich_defaults_overwrites_only_the_active_scheme() {

133:         // Dark active: the dark map gets the native accent, the light map keeps fallback.

135:         assert_eq!(dark.get("color.accent"), Some(&TokenValue::Color(0xFF_112233)));

138: }

1: //! # pathland-render-html
2: //!
3: //! A Pathland renderer that maps opcode frames onto **declarative HTML**
4: //! elements. Like every Pathland renderer it is a pure function of the opcode
5: //! stream: it retains only its own decoded output tree (a cache), never
6: //! application state, and emits `WHAT` the UI is — never layout rects. Native
7: //! browser layout does the positioning.
8: //!
9: //! This is the "server-side render" / remote-projection target (Goal #15): the
10: //! same opcode stream that drives a native backend drives this HTML document.
11: //!
12: //! Frames are **self-contained**: `apply(opcodes, strings)` resolves `SET_TEXT`
13: //! by a *relative* offset into the frame's own string section (no mirrored
14: //! arena), and every rendered element carries a stable `data-pathland-id` so a
15: //! client can hydrate it and apply later deltas in place.
16: 
17: use std::collections::BTreeMap;
18: 
19: use pathland_core::{
20:     Opcode, border_edges, category, component_type, property_id, style, tokens::TokenValue, tree,
21:     value_type,
22: };
23: 
24: mod capi;
25: mod css;
26: 
27: /// A decoded node in the retained description.
28: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
29: pub struct Node {
30:     /// Protocol component type id (see `pathland_core::component_type`).
31:     pub component: u16,
32:     /// Text content set via `STYLE::SET_TEXT`, if any.
33:     pub text: Option<String>,
34:     /// Constraint/style properties (`propertyId → value`).
35:     pub properties: BTreeMap<u16, u32>,
36:     /// `STRING`-typed properties resolved at apply time (`propertyId → text`).
37:     pub strings: BTreeMap<u16, String>,
38:     /// `DESIGN_TOKEN`-typed properties (`propertyId → token path`).
39:     pub token_refs: BTreeMap<u16, String>,
40:     /// Date value from `STYLE::SET_DATE`: (days since epoch, millis of day).
41:     pub date: Option<(i32, u32)>,
42:     /// Child node ids in insertion order.
43:     pub children: Vec<u32>,
44: }
45: 
46: impl Node {
47:     fn new(component: u16) -> Self {
48:         Self {
49:             component,
50:             text: None,
51:             properties: BTreeMap::new(),
52:             strings: BTreeMap::new(),
53:             token_refs: BTreeMap::new(),
54:             date: None,
55:             children: Vec::new(),
56:         }
57:     }
58: 
59:     /// The `SELECTED` checked state, decoded from its `U8` wire value.
60:     fn checked(&self) -> bool {
61:         self.properties
62:             .get(&property_id::SELECTED)
63:             .copied()
64:             .unwrap_or(0)
65:             != 0
66:     }
67: 
68:     /// An `F32` property value, or a default when absent.
69:     fn f32_property(&self, prop: u16, default: f32) -> f32 {
70:         self.properties
71:             .get(&prop)
72:             .copied()
73:             .map(f32::from_bits)
74:             .unwrap_or(default)
75:     }
76: 
77:     /// `CONTENT_MARGINS` (F32), if present.
78:     fn content_margins(&self) -> Option<f32> {
79:         self.properties
80:             .get(&property_id::CONTENT_MARGINS)
81:             .map(|bits| f32::from_bits(*bits))
82:     }
83: 
84:     /// A raw `U32` property value (no f32 reinterpretation), or a default.
85:     fn u32_property(&self, prop: u16, default: u32) -> u32 {
86:         self.properties.get(&prop).copied().unwrap_or(default)
87:     }
88: 
89:     /// If the property carries a `DESIGN_TOKEN` reference, its CSS expression
90:     /// (`var(--pl-…)` or `calc(var(--pl-space-base) * N)` for the generative
91:     /// `space.<N>` family). Resolved at render time — the browser resolves the
92:     /// variable against the token rules in the document head.
93:     fn token_ref(&self, prop: u16) -> Option<String> {
94:         self.token_refs.get(&prop).map(|path| resolve_token_ref(path))
95:     }
96: 
97:     /// Inline CSS for the node. Literal colors and string font-family, plus all
98:     /// **arbitrary-number (dp/point)** styling — spacing, padding, size, offset,
99:     /// rotation, scale, filters, opacity, border-radius, z-index — which render
100:     /// inline because Tailwind can only statically safelist finite enum classes
101:     /// (dp values are unbounded). 1 dp = 1 CSS px (a renderer interpretation).
102:     fn style_css(&self) -> String {
103:         let mut css = String::new();
104:         let f32p = |prop: u16| self.properties.get(&prop).map(|b| f32::from_bits(*b));
105:         let px = |v: f32| format!("{v}px");
106: 
107:         // Colors + font family.
108:         if let Some(v) = self.token_ref(property_id::COLOR) {
109:             css.push_str(&format!("color:{v};"));
110:         } else if let Some(bits) = self.properties.get(&property_id::COLOR) {
111:             css.push_str(&format!("color:{};", rgba(*bits)));
112:         }
113:         if let Some(v) = self.token_ref(property_id::BACKGROUND_COLOR) {
114:             css.push_str(&format!("background-color:{v};"));
115:         } else if let Some(bits) = self.properties.get(&property_id::BACKGROUND_COLOR) {
116:             css.push_str(&format!("background-color:{};", rgba(*bits)));
117:         }
118:         if let Some(family) = self.strings.get(&property_id::FONT_FAMILY) {
119:             css.push_str(&format!("font-family:'{}';", family.replace('\'', "\\'")));
120:         }
121: 
122:         // Layout / distance (dp → px).
123:         if let Some(v) = self.token_ref(property_id::SPACING) {
124:             css.push_str(&format!("gap:{v};"));
125:         } else if let Some(v) = f32p(property_id::SPACING) {
126:             if v > 0.0 {
127:                 css.push_str(&format!("gap:{};", px(v)));
128:             }
129:         }
130:         if let Some(v) = self.token_ref(property_id::CONTENT_MARGINS) {
131:             css.push_str(&format!("padding:{v};"));
132:         } else if let Some(m) = self.content_margins() {
133:             if m > 0.0 {
134:                 css.push_str(&format!("padding:{};", px(m)));
135:             }
136:         }
137:         if let Some(v) = self.token_ref(property_id::PADDING) {
138:             css.push_str(&format!("padding:{v};"));
139:         } else if let Some(v) = f32p(property_id::PADDING) {
140:             if v > 0.0 {
141:                 css.push_str(&format!("padding:{};", px(v)));
142:             }
143:         }
144:         for (prop, side) in [
145:             (property_id::PADDING_TOP, "padding-top"),
146:             (property_id::PADDING_RIGHT, "padding-right"),
147:             (property_id::PADDING_BOTTOM, "padding-bottom"),
148:             (property_id::PADDING_LEFT, "padding-left"),
149:         ] {
150:             if let Some(v) = self.token_ref(prop) {
151:                 css.push_str(&format!("{side}:{v};"));
152:             } else if let Some(v) = f32p(prop) {
153:                 if v > 0.0 {
154:                     css.push_str(&format!("{side}:{};", px(v)));
155:                 }
156:             }
157:         }
158:         // WIDTH/HEIGHT: only non-sentinel (arbitrary) values inline; FILL/HUG are classes.
159:         if let Some(v) = self.token_ref(property_id::WIDTH) {
160:             css.push_str(&format!("width:{v};"));
161:         } else if let Some(v) = f32p(property_id::WIDTH) {
162:             if v != pathland_core::size::FILL && v != pathland_core::size::HUG_CONTENT {
163:                 css.push_str(&format!("width:{};", px(v)));
164:             }
165:         }
166:         if let Some(v) = self.token_ref(property_id::HEIGHT) {
167:             css.push_str(&format!("height:{v};"));
168:         } else if let Some(v) = f32p(property_id::HEIGHT) {
169:             if v != pathland_core::size::FILL && v != pathland_core::size::HUG_CONTENT {
170:                 css.push_str(&format!("height:{};", px(v)));
171:             }
172:         }
173:         if let (Some(x), Some(y)) = (f32p(property_id::OFFSET_X), f32p(property_id::OFFSET_Y)) {
174:             if x != 0.0 || y != 0.0 {
175:                 css.push_str(&format!("transform:translate({}px, {}px);", x, y));
176:             }
177:         } else {
178:             if let Some(v) = f32p(property_id::POSITION_X) {
179:                 if v != 0.0 {
180:                     css.push_str(&format!("left:{};", px(v)));
181:                 }
182:             }
183:             if let Some(v) = f32p(property_id::POSITION_Y) {
184:                 if v != 0.0 {
185:                     css.push_str(&format!("top:{};", px(v)));
186:                 }
187:             }
188:         }
189: 
190:         // Typography (arbitrary size/weight inline).
191:         if let Some(v) = self.token_ref(property_id::FONT_SIZE) {
192:             css.push_str(&format!("font-size:{v};"));
193:         } else if let Some(v) = f32p(property_id::FONT_SIZE) {
194:             if v > 0.0 {
195:                 css.push_str(&format!("font-size:{};", px(v)));
196:             }
197:         }
198:         if let Some(v) = self.token_ref(property_id::FONT_WEIGHT) {
199:             css.push_str(&format!("font-weight:{v};"));
200:         } else if let Some(v) = f32p(property_id::FONT_WEIGHT) {
201:             if v > 0.0 {
202:                 css.push_str(&format!("font-weight:{v};"));
203:             }
204:         }
205:         if let Some(v) = self.token_ref(property_id::BORDER_RADIUS) {
206:             css.push_str(&format!("border-radius:{v};"));
207:         } else if let Some(v) = f32p(property_id::BORDER_RADIUS) {
208:             if v != 0.0 {
209:                 css.push_str(&format!("border-radius:{};", px(v)));
210:             }
211:         }
212: 
213:         // Effects (filters, rotation, scale, shadow, opacity, z-index) inline.
214:         let mut filters: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
215:         if let Some(v) = f32p(property_id::BLUR_RADIUS) {
216:             filters.push(format!("blur({}px)", v));
217:         }
218:         if let Some(v) = f32p(property_id::SATURATION) {
219:             filters.push(format!("saturate({v})"));
220:         }
221:         if let Some(v) = f32p(property_id::CONTRAST) {
222:             filters.push(format!("contrast({v})"));
223:         }
224:         if let Some(v) = f32p(property_id::BRIGHTNESS) {
225:             filters.push(format!("brightness({v})"));
226:         }
227:         if let Some(v) = f32p(property_id::GRAYSCALE) {
228:             filters.push(format!("grayscale({v})"));
229:         }
230:         if let Some(v) = f32p(property_id::HUE_ROTATION) {
231:             filters.push(format!("hue-rotate({v}deg)"));
232:         }
233:         if !filters.is_empty() {
234:             css.push_str(&format!("filter:{};", filters.join(" ")));
235:         }
236:         if let Some(v) = f32p(property_id::ROTATION_DEGREES) {
237:             if v != 0.0 {
238:                 css.push_str(&format!("transform:rotate({v}deg);"));
239:             }
240:         }
241:         if let Some(v) = f32p(property_id::SCALE) {
242:             if v != 1.0 {
243:                 css.push_str(&format!("transform:scale({v});"));
244:             }
245:         }
246:         // Shadow (accumulate x/y/radius/color — simplified to radius+color inline).
247:         if let (Some(r), Some(color_bits)) = (
248:             f32p(property_id::SHADOW_RADIUS),
249:             self.properties.get(&property_id::SHADOW_COLOR).copied(),
250:         ) {
251:             if r != 0.0 {
252:                 let x = f32p(property_id::SHADOW_X).unwrap_or(0.0);
253:                 let y = f32p(property_id::SHADOW_Y).unwrap_or(0.0);
254:                 let color = self
255:                     .token_ref(property_id::SHADOW_COLOR)
256:                     .unwrap_or_else(|| rgba(color_bits));
257:                 css.push_str(&format!("box-shadow:{x}px {y}px {r}px {color};"));
258:             }
259:         }
260:         if let Some(v) = self.token_ref(property_id::OPACITY) {
261:             css.push_str(&format!("opacity:{v};"));
262:         } else if let Some(v) = f32p(property_id::OPACITY) {
263:             if v < 1.0 {
264:                 css.push_str(&format!("opacity:{v};"));
265:             }
266:         }
267:         if let Some(v) = f32p(property_id::Z_INDEX) {
268:             css.push_str(&format!("z-index:{};", v as i32));
269:         }
270: 
271:         // Enum-derived properties (previously Tailwind classes) now inline.
272:         // ALIGNMENT cross-axis (Leading=0, Center=1, Trailing=2, Fill=3 → default stretch).
273:         if let Some(v) = f32p(property_id::ALIGNMENT) {
274:             css.push_str(&format!(
275:                 "align-items:{};",
276:                 match v as u8 {
277:                     0 => "flex-start",
278:                     1 => "center",
279:                     2 => "flex-end",
280:                     _ => "stretch",
281:                 }
282:             ));
283:         }
284:         // TEXT_ALIGNMENT (Leading=0, Center=1, Trailing=2).
285:         if let Some(v) = f32p(property_id::TEXT_ALIGNMENT) {
286:             css.push_str(&format!(
287:                 "text-align:{};",
288:                 match (v as u8).min(2) {
289:                     0 => "left",
290:                     1 => "center",
291:                     _ => "right",
292:                 }
293:             ));
294:         }
295:         // TEXT_CASE (None=0, Uppercase=1, Lowercase=2).
296:         if let Some(v) = f32p(property_id::TEXT_CASE) {
297:             css.push_str(&format!(
298:                 "text-transform:{};",
299:                 match v as u8 {
300:                     1 => "uppercase",
301:                     2 => "lowercase",
302:                     _ => "none",
303:                 }
304:             ));
305:         }
306:         // VISIBLE=0 → hidden.
307:         if let Some(bits) = self.properties.get(&property_id::VISIBLE) {
308:             if *bits == 0 {
309:                 css.push_str("display:none;");
310:             }
311:         }
312:         // FONT_STYLE italic.
313:         if let Some(v) = f32p(property_id::FONT_STYLE) {
314:             if v != 0.0 {
315:                 css.push_str("font-style:italic;");
316:             }
317:         }
318:         // FONT_DESIGN (Default=0, Serif=1, Rounded=2, Monospaced=3).
319:         if let Some(v) = f32p(property_id::FONT_DESIGN) {
320:             css.push_str(&format!(
321:                 "font-family:{};",
322:                 match v as u8 {
323:                     1 => "Georgia, 'Times New Roman', serif",
324:                     2 => "ui-rounded, system-ui, sans-serif",
325:                     3 => "ui-monospace, monospace",
326:                     _ => "inherit",
327:                 }
328:             ));
329:         }
330:         // UNDERLINE / STRIKETHROUGH.
331:         let mut decoration = Vec::new();
332:         if let Some(v) = f32p(property_id::UNDERLINE) {
333:             if v != 0.0 {
334:                 decoration.push("underline");
335:             }
336:         }
337:         if let Some(v) = f32p(property_id::STRIKETHROUGH) {
338:             if v != 0.0 {
339:                 decoration.push("line-through");
340:             }
341:         }
342:         if !decoration.is_empty() {
343:             css.push_str(&format!("text-decoration:{};", decoration.join(" ")));
344:         }
345:         // CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS → overflow hidden.
346:         if let Some(v) = f32p(property_id::CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS) {
347:             if v != 0.0 {
348:                 css.push_str("overflow:hidden;");
349:             }
350:         }
351:         // ALLOWS_HIT_TESTING (inverted: absent = allowed).
352:         if let Some(v) = f32p(property_id::ALLOWS_HIT_TESTING) {
353:             if v == 0.0 {
354:                 css.push_str("pointer-events:none;");
355:             }
356:         }
357:         // COLOR_INVERT.
358:         if let Some(v) = f32p(property_id::COLOR_INVERT) {
359:             if v != 0.0 {
360:                 css.push_str("filter:invert(1);");
361:             }
362:         }
363:         // TRUNCATION_MODE → ellipsis.
364:         if self.properties.contains_key(&property_id::TRUNCATION_MODE) {
365:             css.push_str("text-overflow:ellipsis;overflow:hidden;white-space:nowrap;");
366:         }
367: 
368:         css
369:     }

371:     /// Border CSS, decoded from `BORDER_WIDTH`/`BORDER_COLOR`/`BORDER_RADIUS`/
372:     /// `BORDER_EDGES` (empty when the node has no border).
373:     fn border_style(&self) -> String {
374:         let width = match self.token_ref(property_id::BORDER_WIDTH) {
375:             Some(v) => v,
376:             None => {
377:                 let Some(width_bits) = self.properties.get(&property_id::BORDER_WIDTH) else {
378:                     return String::new();
379:                 };
380:                 format!("{}px", f32::from_bits(*width_bits))
381:             }
382:         };
383:         let color = match self.token_ref(property_id::BORDER_COLOR) {
384:             Some(v) => v,
385:             None => rgba(
386:                 self.properties
387:                     .get(&property_id::BORDER_COLOR)
388:                     .copied()
389:                     .unwrap_or(0xFF00_0000),
390:             ),
391:         };
392:         let edges = self
393:             .properties
394:             .get(&property_id::BORDER_EDGES)
395:             .copied()
396:             .unwrap_or(border_edges::ALL);
397: 
398:         let mut css = String::new();
399:         for (flag, side) in [
400:             (border_edges::TOP, "top"),
401:             (border_edges::LEADING, "left"),
402:             (border_edges::BOTTOM, "bottom"),
403:             (border_edges::TRAILING, "right"),
404:         ] {
405:             if edges & flag != 0 {
406:                 css.push_str(&format!("border-{side}:{width} solid {color};"));
407:             }
408:         }
409:         css
410:     }
411: }

413: /// Unpack a `0xAARRGGBB` color into `(r, g, b, alpha)` where `alpha` is `0..1`.
414: fn unpack_color(argb: u32) -> (u32, u32, u32, f32) {
415:     let r = (argb >> 16) & 0xFF;
416:     let g = (argb >> 8) & 0xFF;
417:     let b = argb & 0xFF;
418:     let a = ((argb >> 24) & 0xFF) as f32 / 255.0;
419:     (r, g, b, a)
420: }
421: 
422: /// A `0xAARRGGBB` color as a CSS `rgba(r,g,b,a)` string.
423: fn rgba(argb: u32) -> String {
424:     let (r, g, b, a) = unpack_color(argb);
425:     format!("rgba({r},{g},{b},{a})")
426: }

428: /// A `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` hint as CSS: `FILL` (-1) → `100%`, `HUG_CONTENT` (-2) →

433:     } else if v == pathland_core::size::HUG_CONTENT {

451: /// Convert days since the Unix epoch (negative = before 1970) to a Gregorian
452: /// `(year, month, day)` using the civil-from-days algorithm.
453: fn days_to_date(days: i32) -> (i32, u32, u32) {
454:     let z = i64::from(days) + 719_468;
455:     let era = if z >= 0 { z } else { z - 146_096 } / 146_097;
456:     let doe = z - era * 146_097;
457:     let yoe = (doe - doe / 1460 + doe / 36524 - doe / 146_096) / 365;
458:     let y = yoe + era * 400;
459:     let doy = doe - (365 * yoe + yoe / 4 - yoe / 100);
460:     let mp = (5 * doy + 2) / 153;
461:     let d = doy - (153 * mp + 2) / 5 + 1;
462:     let m = if mp < 10 { mp + 3 } else { mp - 9 };
463:     let y = if m <= 2 { y + 1 } else { y };
464:     (y as i32, m as u32, d as u32)
465: }

467: /// Millis of day → `(hours, minutes, seconds)`.
468: fn millis_to_hms(millis: u32) -> (u32, u32, u32) {
469:     let total = millis / 1000;
470:     (total / 3600, (total % 3600) / 60, total % 60)
471: }

491: /// ARIA attributes from `ROLE` / `STATE` / `ENABLED`.
492: fn aria_attrs(node: &Node) -> String {
493:     let mut attrs = String::new();
494:     if let Some(bits) = node.properties.get(&property_id::ROLE) {
495:         let role = match f32::from_bits(*bits) as u8 {
496:             1 => "button",
497:             2 => "link",
498:             3 => "heading",
499:             6 => "textbox",
500:             7 => "slider",
501:             8 => "switch",
502:             9 => "checkbox",
503:             12 => "tab",
504:             16 => "scrollbar",
505:             19 => "menuitem",

507:         };
508:         if !role.is_empty() {

529: /// Decode a self-contained snapshot batch (opcodes + string section) into a
530: /// **transient** `id → Node` map. The map lives only for the duration of one
531: /// render call — the renderer retains nothing between calls.
532: fn decode(opcodes: &[Opcode], strings: &[u8]) -> (BTreeMap<u32, Node>, Tokens) {
533:     let mut nodes = BTreeMap::new();
534:     let mut tokens = Tokens::default();
535:     for op in opcodes {
536:         match op.category() {
537:             category::TREE => apply_tree(&mut nodes, op.command(), *op),
538:             category::STYLE => {
539:                 if op.command() == style::SET_DESIGN_TOKEN {
540:                     // Global override: A = arenaRef (token path), B = valueType,
541:                     // C = value (for STRING, an arenaRef to the value string).
542:                     if let Some(path) = strings_str(strings, op.a()) {
543:                         let vt = (op.b() & 0xFF) as u8;
544:                         let value = if vt == value_type::STRING {
545:                             strings_str(strings, op.c())
546:                                 .map(TokenValue::Str)
547:                                 .unwrap_or(TokenValue::U32(0))
548:                         } else {
549:                             TokenValue::from_wire(vt, op.c()).unwrap_or(TokenValue::U32(op.c()))
550:                         };
551:                         tokens.set(&path, vt, value);
552:                     }
553:                 } else {
554:                     apply_style(&mut nodes, op.command(), *op, strings);
555:                 }
556:             }
557:             _ => {}
558:         }
559:     }
560:     (nodes, tokens)
561: }
562: 
563: /// Read a `[u32 len][utf8]` entry from the batch's string section at a relative offset.
564: fn strings_str(strings: &[u8], offset: u32) -> Option<String> {
565:     let offset = offset as usize;
566:     if offset + 4 > strings.len() {
567:         return None;
568:     }
569:     let len = u32::from_le_bytes(strings[offset..offset + 4].try_into().ok()?) as usize;
570:     let start = offset + 4;
571:     if start + len > strings.len() {
572:         return None;
573:     }
574:     std::str::from_utf8(&strings[start..start + len]).ok().map(str::to_owned)
575: }

577: // --- Design tokens (spec/TOKENS.md) ---
578: 
579: /// `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` overrides collected from a snapshot batch. `base` holds
580: /// light tokens (keyed by full path); `dark` holds `dark.`-prefixed overrides
581: /// (keyed by the bare path). Values are resolved [`TokenValue`]s (STRING values
582: /// are resolved from the batch's string section at decode time).
583: #[derive(Debug, Default, Clone)]
584: struct Tokens {
585:     base: BTreeMap<String, (u8, TokenValue)>,
586:     dark: BTreeMap<String, (u8, TokenValue)>,
587: }
588: 
589: impl Tokens {
590:     fn set(&mut self, path: &str, value_type: u8, value: TokenValue) {
591:         if let Some(bare) = path.strip_prefix("dark.") {
592:             self.dark.insert(bare.to_string(), (value_type, value));
593:         } else {
594:             self.base.insert(path.to_string(), (value_type, value));
595:         }
596:     }
597: 
598:     /// Render the overrides as CSS rules: base tokens as `:root` rules, dark
599:     /// overrides inside `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` — the browser
600:     /// resolves the scheme natively, so SSR needs no client scheme knowledge.
601:     fn css(&self) -> String {
602:         let mut css = String::new();
603:         for (path, (vt, value)) in &self.base {
604:             css.push_str(&format!(
605:                 ":root{{{}:{};}}",
606:                 token_to_css_var(path),
607:                 token_css_value(path, *vt, value)
608:             ));
609:         }
610:         if !self.dark.is_empty() {
611:             let rules: String = self
612:                 .dark
613:                 .iter()
614:                 .map(|(path, (vt, value))| {
615:                     format!(":root{{{}:{};}}", token_to_css_var(path), token_css_value(path, *vt, value))
616:                 })
617:                 .collect();
618:             css.push_str(&format!("@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark){{{rules}}}"));
619:         }
620:         css
621:     }
622: }
623: 
624: /// The canonical CSS custom property for a token path: `--pl-` prefix, `.` →
625: /// `-`. The `dark.` scheme prefix is stripped — the dark variant overrides the
626: /// same variable inside the media query (spec/TOKENS.md).
627: fn token_to_css_var(path: &str) -> String {
628:     let name: String = path
629:         .chars()
630:         .map(|c| if c.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || c == '-' || c == '_' { c } else { '-' })
631:         .collect();
632:     format!("--pl-{name}")
633: }
634: 
635: /// Token paths whose F32 values are CSS lengths (emitted with `px`).
636: fn is_length_token(path: &str) -> bool {
637:     if path.starts_with("space.")
638:         || path.starts_with("radius.")
639:         || path.starts_with("border.width.")
640:         || path.starts_with("size.control.")
641:         || path.starts_with("control.padding.")
642:         || path.starts_with("control.height.")
643:     {
644:         return true;
645:     }
646:     if path.starts_with("control.font.") && path.ends_with(".size") {
647:         return true;
648:     }
649:     if path == "font.body.size" || path == "font.caption.size" {
650:         return true;
651:     }
652:     if path.starts_with("font.heading.") && path.ends_with(".size") {
653:         return true;
654:     }
655:     path.starts_with("elevation.")
656:         && (path.ends_with(".radius") || path.ends_with(".x") || path.ends_with(".y") || path.ends_with(".blur"))
657: }
658: 
659: /// Render a token override value as a CSS value string: `STRING` values are
660: /// single-quoted (escaped); `F32` length tokens append `px`.
661: fn token_css_value(path: &str, _value_type: u8, value: &TokenValue) -> String {
662:     match value {
663:         TokenValue::Str(s) => format!("'{}'", s.replace('\\', "\\\\").replace('\'', "\\'")),
664:         TokenValue::Color(argb) => rgba(*argb),
665:         TokenValue::F32(v) => {
666:             if is_length_token(path) {
667:                 format!("{v}px")
668:             } else {
669:                 format!("{v}")
670:             }
671:         }
672:         TokenValue::I32(v) => format!("{v}"),
673:         TokenValue::U32(v) => format!("{v}"),
674:         TokenValue::U8(v) => format!("{v}"),
675:     }
676: }
677: 
678: /// Resolve a `DESIGN_TOKEN` property reference to a CSS expression. The
679: /// generative `space.<N>` family resolves to `calc(var(--pl-space-base) * N)`;
680: /// every other token resolves to `var(--pl-<path>)`.
681: fn resolve_token_ref(path: &str) -> String {
682:     let bare = path.strip_prefix("dark.").unwrap_or(path);
683:     if let Some(rest) = bare.strip_prefix("space.") {
684:         if rest.parse::<f64>().is_ok() {
685:             return format!("calc(var(--pl-space-base) * {rest})");
686:         }
687:     }
688:     format!("var({})", token_to_css_var(bare))
689: }
690: 
691: fn apply_tree(nodes: &mut BTreeMap<u32, Node>, command: u8, op: Opcode) {
692:     match command {
693:         tree::CREATE_NODE => {
694:             let id = op.a();
695:             let component = op.b() as u16;
696:             nodes.insert(id, Node::new(component));
697:         }
698:         tree::DELETE_NODE => {
699:             nodes.remove(&op.a());
700:         }
701:         tree::INSERT_CHILD => {
702:             let (parent, child) = (op.a(), op.b());
703:             if let Some(node) = nodes.get_mut(&parent) {
704:                 node.children.push(child);
705:             }
706:         }
707:         tree::REMOVE_CHILD => {
708:             let (parent, child) = (op.a(), op.b());
709:             if let Some(node) = nodes.get_mut(&parent) {
710:                 node.children.retain(|&c| c != child);
711:             }
712:         }
713:         tree::MOVE_CHILD => {
714:             let (parent, child, index) = (op.a(), op.b(), op.c());
715:             if let Some(node) = nodes.get_mut(&parent) {
716:                 node.children.retain(|&c| c != child);
717:                 let index = (index as usize).min(node.children.len());
718:                 node.children.insert(index, child);
719:             }
720:         }
721:         _ => {}
722:     }
723: }
724: 
725: fn apply_style(nodes: &mut BTreeMap<u32, Node>, command: u8, op: Opcode, strings: &[u8]) {
726:     match command {
727:         style::SET_TEXT => {
728:             if let Some(text) = strings_str(strings, op.b()) {
729:                 if let Some(node) = nodes.get_mut(&op.a()) {
730:                     node.text = Some(text);
731:                 }
732:             }
733:         }
734:         style::SET_PROPERTY => {
735:             let property = (op.b() & 0xFFFF) as u16;
736:             if let Some(node) = nodes.get_mut(&op.a()) {
737:                 let vt = (op.b() >> 16) as u8;
738:                 if vt == value_type::STRING {
739:                     if let Some(text) = strings_str(strings, op.c()) {
740:                         node.strings.insert(property, text);
741:                     }
742:                 } else if vt == value_type::DESIGN_TOKEN {
743:                     // C = arenaRef to the token path; resolved at render time to
744:                     // `var(--pl-…)` / `calc(...)` (see `Node::token_ref`).
745:                     if let Some(path) = strings_str(strings, op.c()) {
746:                         node.token_refs.insert(property, path);
747:                     }
748:                 } else {
749:                     node.properties.insert(property, op.c());
750:                 }
751:             }
752:         }
753:         style::SET_DATE => {
754:             if let Some(node) = nodes.get_mut(&op.a()) {
755:                 // B = days since epoch (I32), C = millis of day (U32).
756:                 node.date = Some((op.b() as i32, op.c()));
757:             }
758:         }
759:         _ => {}
760:     }
761: }

763: /// A **stateless, streaming** HTML renderer. Each render call decodes a
764: /// self-contained snapshot batch into a transient map, walks it once, and
765: /// streams HTML text out — zero state retained across calls. A pure function
766: /// of the opcode stream (Renderer Statelessness).
767: #[derive(Debug, Default, Clone, Copy)]
768: pub struct HtmlRenderer;
769: 
770: impl HtmlRenderer {
771:     /// Create a renderer (stateless; the same value serves every render).
772:     #[must_use]
773:     pub fn new() -> Self {
774:         Self
775:     }
776: 
777:     /// Render the subtree rooted at `root` as a full HTML document.
778:     #[must_use]
779:     pub fn render_document(&self, opcodes: &[Opcode], strings: &[u8], root: u32) -> String {
780:         let (nodes, tokens) = decode(opcodes, strings);
781:         let body = render_node(&nodes, root);
782:         // Token overrides render as their own `<style data-pathland-tokens>`
783:         // element AFTER the built-in block so their `:root` variables win the
784:         // cascade (same specificity, later wins) — matching the JS DOM client's
785:         // `style[data-pathland-tokens]` element. No overrides → no element.
786:         let token_rules = tokens.css();
787:         let token_style = if token_rules.is_empty() {
788:             String::new()
789:         } else {
790:             format!("<style data-pathland-tokens>{token_rules}</style>\n")
791:         };
792:         format!(
793:             "<!DOCTYPE html>\n<html>\n<head>\n<meta charset=\"utf-8\">\n\
794:              <meta name=\"viewport\" content=\"width=device-width, initial-scale=1\">\n\
795:              <title>Pathland</title>\n\

1: //! # Pathland GTK4 desktop demo
2: //!
3: //! A native GTK4 app demonstrating Pathland's **zero-copy shared-memory ring**
4: //! and the shared **GTK renderer** (`pathland-render-gtk`).
5: //!
6: //! The developer authors the UI with the SwiftUI-style DSL; the diff emitter in
7: //! `pathland-core` emits declarative 16-byte opcodes into the shared ring, and
8: //! the `pathland-render-gtk` renderer maps them onto native GTK widgets. The demo
9: //! never touches GTK/glib/pango directly — it only drives Pathland and the
10: //! renderer.
11: //!
12: //! Interaction is declared with `.on_tap_gesture(...)` on any view; raw pointer
13: //! events round-trip through the shared ring and are turned back into taps by
14: //! the app-side [`TapRecognizer`](pathland_view::TapRecognizer).
15: 
16: use std::cell::RefCell;
17: use std::collections::BTreeMap;
18: use std::rc::Rc;
19: use std::time::Instant;
20: 
21: use pathland_engine::Engine;
22: use pathland_core::{listener, size};
23: use pathland_core_transport::RingTransport;
24: use pathland_view::{assign_ids, button, hstack, text, vstack, Align, Color, Node, View, ViewExt};
25: 
26: const APP_ID: &str = "org.pathland.GtkDemo";
27: 
28: /// node id → tap callback, collected from the built tree after `assign_ids`.
29: type TapHandlers = BTreeMap<u32, Rc<RefCell<dyn FnMut() + 'static>>>;
30: 
31: /// Build the DSL tree for the current counter value. This is the developer's
32: /// authoring surface.
33: fn build_tree(count: &Rc<RefCell<u32>>) -> Node {
34:     let tap_count = count.clone();
35:     vstack![
36:         hstack![
37:             text(format!("Count: {}", *count.borrow()).as_str())
38:                 .frame(Some(size::FILL), None, None),
39:             button("Increment").on_tap_gesture(move || *tap_count.borrow_mut() += 1),
40:         ]
41:         .spacing(8.0)
42:         .padding(16.0),
43:         text("Pathland · GTK4 · shared ring").foreground_style(Color::argb(0xFF_888888)),
44:         // A non-button view (Text) declaring raw pointer listeners — proving any
45:         // element can emit events via the `EVENT_LISTENERS` property.
46:         text("I am a Text with raw pointer listeners")
47:             .pointer_events(listener::POINTER_DOWN | listener::POINTER_UP)
48:             .foreground_style(Color::argb(0xFF_0000AA)),
49:         vstack![
50:             text("short"),
51:             text("a much longer label"),
52:             text("x"),
53:         ]
54:         .spacing(4.0)
55:         .padding(16.0)
56:         .frame(None, None, Some(Align::Center)),
57:     ]
58:     .spacing(12.0)
59:     .padding(24.0)
60:     .build()
61: }
62: 
63: fn main() {
64:     let engine = Rc::new(RefCell::new(Engine::new()));
65:     let ring = Rc::new(RefCell::new(RingTransport::new()));
66:     let count = Rc::new(RefCell::new(0u32));
67:     let handlers = Rc::new(RefCell::new(TapHandlers::new()));
68: 
69:     // Build + emit the current tree, refreshing the id → tap-callback map.
70:     let emit = {
71:         let engine = engine.clone();
72:         let ring = ring.clone();
73:         let count = count.clone();
74:         let handlers = handlers.clone();
75:         move || {
76:             let mut tree = build_tree(&count);
77:             assign_ids(&mut tree, &mut 1);
78:             let mut h = handlers.borrow_mut();
79:             h.clear();
80:             pathland_view::collect_tap_handlers(&tree, &mut *h);
81:             drop(h);
82: 
83:             let mut ring_ref = ring.borrow_mut();
84:             let mut guest = ring_ref.producer();
85:             guest.begin_frame();
86:             engine.borrow_mut().emit(&tree, &mut guest).ok();
87:             guest.end_frame();
88:         }
89:     };
90: 
91:     // Initial frame before the renderer starts pumping.
92:     emit();
93: 
94:     // Hand the renderer the shared ring and a wake handler. The renderer writes
95:     // native inputs as EVENT opcodes into the ring and wakes us; we drain the
96:     // ring, run the taps through the recognizer, invoke the matching callback,
97:     // and re-emit. The renderer's idle pump applies the delta.
98:     pathland_gtk::run(APP_ID, "Pathland GTK4 Demo", ring.clone(), {
99:         let emit = emit;
100:         let handlers = handlers.clone();
101:         let start = Instant::now();
102:         let mut recognizer = pathland_view::TapRecognizer::new();
103:         move |ring| {
104:             let events = ring.borrow_mut().drain_events();
105:             let now_ms = start.elapsed().as_millis() as u64;
106:             let mut tapped = false;
107:             for ev in &events {
108:                 // Platform back (Escape/back key) arrives as a global NAVIGATE
109:                 // request with no URL. There is no Rust router yet, so this is
110:                 // surfaced to the console to prove the event reached the app.
111:                 if matches!(ev, pathland_core::Event::Navigate { url: None }) {
112:                     eprintln!("[demo] NAVIGATE back requested");
113:                 }
114:                 if let Some(target) = recognizer.feed(ev, now_ms) {
115:                     if let Some(handler) = handlers.borrow().get(&target) {
116:                         let mut cb = handler.borrow_mut();
117:                         (&mut *cb)();
118:                         tapped = true;
119:                     }
120:                 }
121:             }
122:             if tapped {
123:                 emit();
124:             }
125:         }
126:     });
127: }

1: //! C ABI for the Pathland native host.
2: //!
3: //! Foreign host languages (Swift, Java, C#, …) link this `cdylib` and call the
4: //! `pathland_native_*` functions. The surface is the **flat world** — no
5: //! per-component wrappers — and the ring is exposed as a raw pointer + length so
6: //! the foreign driver reads opcodes **in place** (zero-copy).
7: //!
8: //! ```c
9: //! void* h = pathland_native_create();
10: //! pathland_native_create_node(h, 1, 2);            // 2 = vstack
11: //! pathland_native_create_node(h, 2, 3);            // 3 = text
12: //! pathland_native_set_text(h, 2, "Hello");
13: //! pathland_native_insert_child(h, 1, 2, UINT32_MAX);
14: //! pathland_native_emit(h);
15: //! // read opcodes from pathland_native_ring_ptr(h) (header at offset 0)
16: //! pathland_native_destroy(h);
17: //! ```
18: 
19: use std::ffi::{c_char, c_void, CStr};

21: use pathland_engine::{SignalId, SignalValue};

23: use super::{component_from_id, NativeHost};

25: /// Opaque handle to a [`NativeHost`].
26: pub type HostHandle = *mut c_void;
27: 
28: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
29: // Lifetime
30: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
31: 
32: /// Create a native host over a fresh zero-copy shared ring. Returns an opaque
33: /// handle (non-null on success).
34: #[no_mangle]
35: pub extern "C" fn pathland_native_create() -> HostHandle {
36:     let host = Box::new(NativeHost::new());
37:     Box::into_raw(host) as HostHandle
38: }
39: 
40: /// Destroy a native host previously created by [`pathland_native_create`].
41: #[no_mangle]
42: pub unsafe extern "C" fn pathland_native_destroy(host: HostHandle) {
43:     if !host.is_null() {
44:         drop(Box::from_raw(host as *mut NativeHost));
45:     }
46: }
47: 
48: fn as_host<'a>(host: HostHandle) -> &'a mut NativeHost {
49:     unsafe { &mut *(host as *mut NativeHost) }
50: }
51: 
52: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
53: // Flat builder (variants as raw u32)
54: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
55: 
56: /// `component_id` here is the raw protocol component id (hstack=1, vstack=2,
57: /// text=3, button=4, spacer=8). Returns 1 on success, 0 on bad component.
58: #[no_mangle]
59: pub unsafe extern "C" fn pathland_native_create_node(
60:     host: HostHandle,
61:     id: u32,
62:     component: u32,
63: ) -> u8 {
64:     let Some(component) = component_from_id(component) else {
65:         return 0;
66:     };
67:     as_host(host).create_node(id, component);
68:     1
69: }
70: 
71: #[no_mangle]
72: pub unsafe extern "C" fn pathland_native_insert_child(
73:     host: HostHandle,
74:     parent: u32,
75:     child: u32,
76:     index: u32,
77: ) -> u8 {
78:     as_host(host).insert_child(parent, child, index);
79:     1
80: }
81: 
82: #[no_mangle]
83: pub unsafe extern "C" fn pathland_native_remove_child(host: HostHandle, parent: u32, child: u32) -> u8 {
84:     as_host(host).remove_child(parent, child);
85:     1
86: }

88: /// Set a node's text content from a NUL-terminated UTF-8 C string.
89: #[no_mangle]

91:     host: HostHandle,
92:     id: u32,
93:     text: *const c_char,

95:     if text.is_null() {
96:         return 0;
97:     }
98:     let text = CStr::from_ptr(text).to_string_lossy().into_owned();

132: /// Emit the retained tree as opcodes into the shared ring. Returns 1 if a frame
133: /// was written.

135: pub unsafe extern "C" fn pathland_native_emit(host: HostHandle) -> u8 {
136:     if as_host(host).emit() {

138:     } else {
139:         0
140:     }

148: /// foreign driver can read opcodes in place. Never null; the header layout is
149: /// the stable wire layout in `spec/OPCODE.md` (frameCount/readCursor/
150: /// writeCursor/ringOffset/arenaOffset at their documented offsets).
151: #[no_mangle]

153:     let host = as_host(host);
154:     host.ring_buffer().as_ptr()
155: }

158: #[no_mangle]

160:     let host = as_host(host);
161:     host.ring_buffer().len()
162: }
163: 
164: /// Convenience: return the total buffer length of the default layout.
165: #[no_mangle]
166: pub unsafe extern "C" fn pathland_native_layout_bytes(host: HostHandle) -> usize {
167:     let host = as_host(host);
168:     host.layout().total_bytes()
169: }
170: 
171: /// Read the root node id (u32_MAX = none).
172: #[no_mangle]
173: pub unsafe extern "C" fn pathland_native_root_id(host: HostHandle) -> u32 {
174:     as_host(host).root_id().unwrap_or(u32::MAX)
175: }
176: 
177: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
178: // Raw-input events (host → guest)
179: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
180: 
181: /// Drain pending raw-input events written by a renderer into the host → guest
182: /// event ring, writing each as its raw 16-byte `EVENT` opcode
183: /// (`[category][command][flags:u16][A:u32][B:u32][C:u32]`, little-endian) into
184: /// `out`. Returns the number of events written (≤ `max`).
185: ///
186: /// `out` must point to at least `max * 16` writable bytes. This is the generic
187: /// event path: the renderer only writes `EVENT` opcodes; the host drains them
188: /// here, symmetric with how a driver reads frame opcodes via
189: /// [`pathland_native_ring_ptr`].
190: #[no_mangle]
191: pub unsafe extern "C" fn pathland_native_drain_events(
192:     host: HostHandle,
193:     out: *mut u8,
194:     max: u32,
195: ) -> u32 {
196:     if out.is_null() || max == 0 {
197:         return 0;
198:     }
199:     let events = as_host(host).drain_events();
200:     let n = events.len().min(max as usize);
201:     for (i, ev) in events.into_iter().take(n).enumerate() {
202:         let bytes = ev.encode().to_bytes();
203:         // SAFETY: `out` points to ≥ max*16 writable bytes; we write ≤ max slots.
204:         std::ptr::copy_nonoverlapping(bytes.as_ptr(), out.add(i * 16), 16);
205:     }
206:     n as u32
207: }

1: //! # pathland-core-capi
2: //!
3: //! The minimal C ABI for the Pathland SPSC ring buffer + 16-byte opcode engine,
4: //! built as `libpathland_core` (a `cdylib`). Foreign hosts (Java FFM, Swift,
5: //! C#, …) construct the 16-byte opcodes themselves, allocate variable-length
6: //! strings into the bump arena, and push them into the shared ring **in
7: //! place** — the engine stays in Rust, the retained tree / diff stays in the
8: //! host language.
9: //!
10: //! ```c
11: //! void* h = pathland_core_create();
12: //! pathland_core_begin_frame(h);
13: //! uint8_t op[16] = { 0x01, 0x01, 0, 0, 1,0,0,0, 2,0,0,0, 0,0,0,0 };
14: //! pathland_ring_buffer_push(h, op);   // TREE::CREATE_NODE, id 1, vstack
15: //! pathland_core_end_frame(h);
16: //! // read opcodes zero-copy from pathland_core_ring_ptr(h)
17: //! pathland_core_destroy(h);
18: //! ```
19: //!
20: //! Opcode layout (little-endian): `[Category u8][Command u8][Flags u16][A u32]
21: //! [B u32][C u32]` — see `spec/OPCODE.md`.
22: 
23: use plcore::{Opcode, OPCODE_SIZE};
24: use pathland_core_transport::RingTransport;
25: 
26: /// Opaque handle to a ring host.
27: pub type CoreHandle = *mut std::ffi::c_void;

30: struct CoreHost {
31:     ring: RingTransport,
32: }

34: fn as_host<'a>(handle: CoreHandle) -> &'a mut CoreHost {
35:     assert!(!handle.is_null(), "pathland_core: null handle");
36:     // SAFETY: handles come only from `pathland_core_create`.
37:     unsafe { &mut *(handle as *mut CoreHost) }

39: 
40: /// Read a 16-byte opcode from a foreign pointer.
41: fn opcode_from_ptr(opcode: *const u8) -> Option<Opcode> {
42:     if opcode.is_null() {
43:         return None;
44:     }
45:     // SAFETY: the caller guarantees `opcode` points to ≥ 16 readable bytes.
46:     let slice = unsafe { std::slice::from_raw_parts(opcode, OPCODE_SIZE) };
47:     let arr: [u8; OPCODE_SIZE] = slice.try_into().ok()?;
48:     Some(Opcode::from_bytes(&arr))

52: // Lifetime
53: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

56: /// handle (non-null on success).

70:         drop(Box::from_raw(handle as *mut CoreHost));

75: // Ring (guest → host)

78: /// Push one raw 16-byte opcode into the shared ring at `writeCursor`, advancing
79: /// it. Returns 1 on success, 0 when the ring is full or `opcode` is null.
80: #[no_mangle]
81: pub unsafe extern "C" fn pathland_ring_buffer_push(handle: CoreHandle, opcode: *const u8) -> u8 {
82:     let Some(op) = opcode_from_ptr(opcode) else {
83:         return 0;
84:     };
85:     let mut guest = as_host(handle).ring.producer();
86:     u8::from(guest.push_opcode(op).is_ok())

89: /// Allocate `len` bytes into the bump arena, returning the absolute arena
90: /// offset (a `u32` reference for `STYLE::SET_TEXT` / `STRING` property values).
91: /// Returns `u32::MAX` when the arena is full or `bytes` is null.
92: #[no_mangle]
93: pub unsafe extern "C" fn pathland_core_arena_alloc(
94:     handle: CoreHandle,
95:     bytes: *const u8,
96:     len: u32,
97: ) -> u32 {
98:     if bytes.is_null() {
99:         return u32::MAX;
100:     }
101:     // SAFETY: the caller guarantees `bytes` points to ≥ `len` readable bytes.
102:     let slice = unsafe { std::slice::from_raw_parts(bytes, len as usize) };

119: }

132:     as_host(handle).ring.buffer().as_ptr()
133: }

136: #[no_mangle]
137: pub unsafe extern "C" fn pathland_core_ring_len(handle: CoreHandle) -> u64 {

139: }

142: /// renderer, which pumps it in place). Returns NULL for a null handle.
143: ///
144: /// The caller must not destroy the core handle until the consumer is done with
145: /// the ring. The pointer is only valid inside this process.
146: #[no_mangle]
147: pub unsafe extern "C" fn pathland_core_ring_mut(handle: CoreHandle) -> *mut RingTransport {
148:     if handle.is_null() {
149:         return std::ptr::null_mut();
150:     }
151:     &mut as_host(handle).ring
152: }
153: 
154: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
155: // Events (host → guest)
156: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
157: 
158: /// Drain pending raw `EVENT`-category opcodes from the host → guest event ring,
159: /// copying each 16-byte opcode into `out`. Returns the number of events
160: /// written (≤ `max`). `out` must point to ≥ `max * 16` writable bytes.
161: #[no_mangle]
162: pub unsafe extern "C" fn pathland_core_drain_events(
163:     handle: CoreHandle,
164:     out: *mut u8,
165:     max: u32,
166: ) -> u32 {
167:     if out.is_null() || max == 0 {
168:         return 0;
169:     }
170:     let mut guest = as_host(handle).ring.producer();
171:     let events = guest.drain_event_opcodes();
172:     let n = events.len().min(max as usize);
173:     for (i, op) in events.into_iter().take(n).enumerate() {
174:         let bytes = op.to_bytes();

176:         std::ptr::copy_nonoverlapping(bytes.as_ptr(), out.add(i * 16), 16);
177:     }

179: }

187:     };

190: }

1: //! # pathland-view-native
2: //!
3: //! Native (non-WASM) projection of the Pathland flat world, exposed over both a
4: //! Rust API and a C ABI for foreign host languages (Swift / Java / C# / …).
5: //!
6: //! This is the **cross-language, zero-copy** path: a host links this crate as a
7: //! native library (or a `cdylib` and its `pathland_native_*` C functions), drives
8: //! the retained tree with the flat `builder`/`engine` operations, and reads
9: //! opcodes from the **shared-memory ring in place** — no serialization, no batch,
10: //! no WASM.
11: //!
12: //! The surface is the flat `builder`/`engine` world over a native shared-memory
13: //! transport.
14: 
15: use std::collections::{BTreeMap, HashMap};
16: 
17: use pathland_engine::{Engine, SignalId, SignalValue};
18: use pathland_core::{component_type, property_id, MemoryLayout};
19: use pathland_core_transport::{
20:     DriverTransport, FrameSource, OpcodeBatch, RingTransport, TransportError,
21: };
22: use pathland_view::{component_type_id, Node};
23: 
24: mod capi;
25: 
26: /// A flat node in the host's retained tree (id → node).
27: #[derive(Clone)]
28: pub struct FlatNode {
29:     pub id: u32,
30:     pub view_component: pathland_view::Component,
31:     pub properties: BTreeMap<u16, u32>,
32:     /// A signal the node's text is bound to (overrides the component text).
33:     pub text_binding: Option<SignalId>,
34:     /// Property signals (propertyId → signal), overriding static properties.
35:     pub property_bindings: BTreeMap<u16, SignalId>,
36:     pub parent: Option<u32>,
37:     pub children: Vec<u32>,
38: }
39: 
40: /// The native host: owns the retained tree, the diff engine, and the shared
41: /// zero-copy ring.
42: pub struct NativeHost {
43:     nodes: HashMap<u32, FlatNode>,
44:     engine: Engine,
45:     ring: RingTransport,
46: }
47: 
48: /// Safe, checked operations returning `()` (used by the C shim).
49: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
50: pub enum HostError {
51:     /// The operation referenced a missing node.
52:     NotFound,
53: }
54: 
55: impl NativeHost {
56:     /// Create a host with a fresh shared ring (default layout).
57:     pub fn new() -> Self {
58:         Self {
59:             nodes: HashMap::new(),
60:             engine: Engine::new(),
61:             ring: RingTransport::new(),
62:         }
63:     }
64: 
65:     /// Create a host over a caller-provided ring buffer + layout.
66:     pub fn with_buffer(mem: Vec<u8>, layout: MemoryLayout) -> Self {
67:         Self {
68:             nodes: HashMap::new(),
69:             engine: Engine::new(),
70:             ring: RingTransport::with_buffer(mem, layout),
71:         }
72:     }
73: 
74:     /// Create (or reset) a node with a host-supplied stable id.
75:     pub fn create_node(&mut self, id: u32, component: pathland_view::Component) {
76:         let entry = self.nodes.entry(id).or_insert(FlatNode {
77:             id,
78:             view_component: component.clone(),
79:             properties: BTreeMap::new(),
80:             text_binding: None,
81:             property_bindings: BTreeMap::new(),
82:             parent: None,
83:             children: Vec::new(),
84:         });
85:         entry.view_component = component;
86:         entry.properties.clear();
87:         entry.text_binding = None;
88:         entry.property_bindings.clear();
89:     }
90: 
91:     /// Insert `child` into `parent` at `index` (u32::MAX appends).
92:     pub fn insert_child(&mut self, parent: u32, child: u32, index: u32) {
93:         if let Some(p) = self.nodes.get_mut(&parent) {
94:             let idx = if index == u32::MAX {
95:                 p.children.len()
96:             } else {
97:                 (index as usize).min(p.children.len())
98:             };
99:             if !p.children.contains(&child) {
100:                 p.children.insert(idx, child);
101:             }
102:         }
103:         if let Some(c) = self.nodes.get_mut(&child) {
104:             c.parent = Some(parent);
105:         }
106:     }
107: 
108:     /// Remove `child` from `parent`.
109:     pub fn remove_child(&mut self, parent: u32, child: u32) {
110:         if let Some(p) = self.nodes.get_mut(&parent) {
111:             p.children.retain(|c| *c != child);
112:         }
113:         if let Some(c) = self.nodes.get_mut(&child) {
114:             c.parent = None;
115:         }
116:     }
117: 
118:     /// Set a node's text content.
119:     pub fn set_text(&mut self, id: u32, text: &str) {
120:         if let Some(node) = self.nodes.get_mut(&id) {
121:             match &mut node.view_component {
122:                 pathland_view::Component::Text { text: t } => *t = text.into(),
123:                 pathland_view::Component::Button { label } => *label = text.into(),
124:                 _ => {}
125:             }
126:         }
127:     }
128: 
129:     /// Set a constraint/style property (raw value bits; valueType derived from
130:     /// the property id).
131:     pub fn set_property(&mut self, id: u32, prop: u16, value: u32) {
132:         if let Some(node) = self.nodes.get_mut(&id) {
133:             node.properties.insert(prop, value);
134:         }
135:     }
136: 
137:     /// Set a float property (stores `f32` bit pattern).
138:     pub fn set_property_f32(&mut self, id: u32, prop: u16, value: f32) {
139:         self.set_property(id, prop, value.to_bits());
140:     }
141: 
142:     /// Bind a node's text to a signal (the signal's `Str` value wins over any
143:     /// static text). Returns `true` if the node exists.
144:     pub fn bind_text(&mut self, id: u32, signal: SignalId) -> bool {
145:         if let Some(node) = self.nodes.get_mut(&id) {
146:             node.text_binding = Some(signal);
147:             true
148:         } else {
149:             false
150:         }
151:     }
152: 
153:     /// Bind a node's property to a signal. Returns `true` if the node exists.
154:     pub fn bind_property(&mut self, id: u32, prop: u16, signal: SignalId) -> bool {
155:         if let Some(node) = self.nodes.get_mut(&id) {
156:             node.property_bindings.insert(prop, signal);
157:             true
158:         } else {
159:             false
160:         }
161:     }
162: 
163:     /// Create a new signal with an initial value.
164:     pub fn create_signal(&mut self, value: SignalValue) -> SignalId {
165:         self.engine.create_signal(value)
166:     }
167: 
168:     /// Read a signal's current value.
169:     pub fn get_signal(&self, id: SignalId) -> Option<SignalValue> {
170:         self.engine.get_signal(id).cloned()
171:     }
172: 
173:     /// Replace a signal's value, re-emitting only the nodes that depend on it.
174:     ///
175:     /// Writes `SET_PROPERTY` / `SET_TEXT` deltas into the shared ring. Returns
176:     /// `true` if any opcodes were written.
177:     pub fn set_signal(&mut self, id: SignalId, value: SignalValue) -> bool {
178:         let mut guest = self.ring.producer();
179:         guest.begin_frame();
180:         let n = self.engine.set_signal(id, value, &mut guest).unwrap_or(0);
181:         guest.end_frame();
182:         n > 0
183:     }
184: 
185:     /// Emit the retained tree as opcodes into the shared ring.
186:     ///
187:     /// Returns `true` if a frame was written (i.e. the tree is non-empty).
188:     pub fn emit(&mut self) -> bool {
189:         let root = self.root_id().and_then(|r| self.materialize(r));
190:         if let Some(root) = root {
191:             let mut guest = self.ring.producer();
192:             guest.begin_frame();
193:             let _ = self.engine.emit(&root, &mut guest);
194:             guest.end_frame();
195:             true
196:         } else {
197:             false
198:         }
199:     }
200: 
201:     /// The ring's linear-memory buffer (for embedding / FFI).
202:     pub fn ring_buffer(&self) -> &[u8] {
203:         self.ring.buffer()
204:     }
205:

207:     pub fn take_ring(self) -> RingTransport {

225:     /// Materialize a `pathland_view::Node` subtree rooted at `id`.
226:     fn materialize(&self, id: u32) -> Option<Node> {
227:         let flat = self.nodes.get(&id)?.clone();
228:         let mut node = Node::from_component(&flat.view_component);
229:         node.id = flat.id;
230:         node.properties = flat.properties.clone();
231:         node.text_binding = flat.text_binding;
232:         node.property_bindings = flat.property_bindings.clone();
233:         for child_id in &flat.children {
234:             if let Some(child) = self.materialize(*child_id) {
235:                 node.children.push(child);

7: /// Opcode categories (`Category` field, u8).

10:     pub const TREE: u8 = 0x01;

12:     /// (spacing, padding, alignment, …) that native renderers use to lay out
13:     /// native elements. The engine does NOT emit rects.
14:     pub const STYLE: u8 = 0x02;

16:     pub const EVENT: u8 = 0x03;

18:     pub const META: u8 = 0x04;

92: impl<'a> SharedHeader<'a> {

198:     pub fn begin_frame(&mut self) {
199:         self.frame_start = header::get_u32(self.header, OFF_WRITE_CURSOR);

203:     pub fn pending(&self) -> usize {
204:         let write = header::get_u32(self.header, OFF_WRITE_CURSOR);
205:         let mask = self.mask() as u32;
206:         (write.wrapping_sub(self.frame_start) & mask) as usize
207:     }

209:     /// End the frame: increments `frameCount`.
210:     pub fn end_frame(&mut self) {
211:         let count = header::get_u32(self.header, OFF_FRAME_COUNT);
212:         header::set_u32(self.header, OFF_FRAME_COUNT, count.wrapping_add(1));
213:     }
214: 
215:     /// Total frames produced so far.
216:     pub fn frame_count(&self) -> u32 {
217:         header::get_u32(self.header, OFF_FRAME_COUNT)
218:     }

364:     /// Drain all pending raw-input events written by the host into the event
365:     /// ring, decoding each 16-byte `EVENT` opcode into a typed [`Event`].
366:     ///
367:     /// The guest (app/engine) polls this to receive renderer-reported inputs.
368:     pub fn drain_events(&mut self) -> Vec<Event> {
369:         let mask = self.mask();
370:         let ops = ring_fn::read_events(&self.event_slots, self.header, mask);
371:         ops.into_iter()
372:             .filter_map(|op| crate::events::decode_event(&op, self.event_arena))
373:             .collect()
374:     }

377:     /// their 16-byte wire form (no decoding). Used by foreign hosts that want
378:     /// the raw bytes.
379:     pub fn drain_event_opcodes(&mut self) -> Vec<Opcode> {
380:         let mask = self.mask();
381:         ring_fn::read_events(&self.event_slots, self.header, mask)
382:     }

385:     pub fn event_arena_cursor(&self) -> u32 {
386:         header::get_u32(self.header, memory::OFF_EVENT_ARENA_CURSOR)
387:     }

390:     ///
391:     /// This is the host-side write (the renderer reporting an input). Exposed
392:     /// here (guest can hold the ring too) so a C-ABI shim can inject raw event
393:     /// opcodes without round-tripping through the typed [`Event`] enum.
394:     pub fn push_event_opcode(&mut self, op: Opcode) -> Result<(), RingError> {
395:         ring_fn::push_event(self.event_slots, self.header, self.mask(), &op)
396:     }

399: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
400: // Host (consumer)
401: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
402: 
403: /// A completed frame produced by the guest: a sequence of opcodes plus arena
404: /// access.
405: ///
406: /// `Frame` is the **transport seam**: both the shared-memory ring (`Host`) and
407: /// network batch decoders produce frame views, so consumers such as
408: /// `RenderTree::apply_frame` work identically regardless of origin.
409: pub struct Frame<'a> {
410:     slots: &'a [u8],
411:     arena: &'a [u8],
412:     start: usize,
413:     end: usize,
414: }
415: 
416: impl<'a> Frame<'a> {
417:     /// Construct a frame view over contiguous 16-byte opcode slots plus an
418:     /// arena region (`start`/`end` are byte offsets into `slots`).
419:     ///
420:     /// Used by transport backends to produce `Frame` views over their own
421:     /// buffers; `Host` builds these internally from the ring.
422:     pub fn from_parts(slots: &'a [u8], arena: &'a [u8], start: usize, end: usize) -> Self {
423:         Self {
424:             slots,
425:             arena,
426:             start,
427:             end,
428:         }
429:     }
430: 
431:     /// Iterate the opcodes in this frame, in order.
432:     pub fn opcodes(&self) -> FrameIter<'a> {
433:         FrameIter {
434:             slots: self.slots,
435:             cursor: self.start,
436:             end: self.end,
437:         }
438:     }
439: 
440:     /// Number of opcodes in the frame.
441:     pub fn len(&self) -> usize {
442:         (self.end - self.start) / Opcode::SIZE
443:     }
444: 
445:     pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
446:         self.len() == 0
447:     }
448: 
449:     /// Read an arena entry by offset (see `Guest::alloc` / `Guest::alloc_str`).
450:     pub fn arena_get(&self, offset: u32) -> Result<&'a [u8], ArenaError> {
451:         arena_fn::get(self.arena, offset)
452:     }
453: 
454:     /// Read an arena string by offset.
455:     pub fn arena_str(&self, offset: u32) -> Result<&'a str, ArenaError> {
456:         arena_fn::get_str(self.arena, offset)
457:     }
458: 
459:     /// The full arena region (for transport serialization of arena deltas).
460:     pub fn arena(&self) -> &'a [u8] {
461:         self.arena
462:     }
463: }
464: 
465: /// Iterator over the opcodes in a `Frame`.
466: pub struct FrameIter<'a> {
467:     slots: &'a [u8],
468:     cursor: usize,
469:     end: usize,
470: }
471: 
472: impl<'a> Iterator for FrameIter<'a> {
473:     type Item = Opcode;
474: 
475:     fn next(&mut self) -> Option<Opcode> {
476:         if self.cursor >= self.end {
477:             return None;
478:         }
479:         let bytes: [u8; 16] = self.slots[self.cursor..self.cursor + 16].try_into().unwrap();
480:         self.cursor += 16;
481:         Some(Opcode::from_bytes(&bytes))
482:     }
483: }
484: 
485: /// Consumer side: the host renderer reading completed frames.
486: ///
487: /// SPSC contract: the host never reads past the producer's published
488: /// `writeCursor`, and the producer never overwrites an unconsumed `readCursor`.
489: /// If the host is slow, multiple produced frames are coalesced into one `Frame`
490: /// (opcodes remain in order); the `frameCount` simply signals "new data".
491: pub struct Host<'a> {
492:     header: &'a mut [u8],
493:     slots: &'a [u8],
494:     /// Host → guest event ring (host writes raw inputs here).
495:     event_slots: &'a mut [u8],
496:     arena: &'a [u8],
497:     /// Host → guest event arena (host-owned bump; the host writes event string
498:     /// payloads here, e.g. `TEXT_CHANGED` text over the shared ring).
499:     event_arena: &'a mut [u8],
500:     /// Number of frames already consumed by this host view.
501:     consumed: u32,
502: }
503: 
504: impl<'a> Host<'a> {
505:     /// Create a host view over the linear memory.
506:     pub fn new(mem: &'a mut [u8], layout: &MemoryLayout) -> Self {
507:         let (header, rest) = mem.split_at_mut(memory::HEADER_SIZE);
508:         let (slots, rest) = rest.split_at_mut(layout.ring_bytes());
509:         let (event_slots, rest) = rest.split_at_mut(layout.event_ring_bytes());
510:         let (arena, event_arena) = rest.split_at_mut(layout.arena_bytes);
511:         let slots: &'a [u8] = slots;
512:         let arena: &'a [u8] = arena;
513:         Self {
514:             header,
515:             slots,
516:             event_slots,
517:             arena,
518:             event_arena,
519:             consumed: 0,
520:         }
521:     }
522: 
523:     /// Total frames produced by the guest (for diagnostics).
524:     pub fn frame_count(&self) -> u32 {
525:         header::get_u32(self.header, OFF_FRAME_COUNT)
526:     }
527: 
528:     /// Consume all frames produced since the last call, advancing `readCursor`.
529:     ///
530:     /// Returns at most one `Frame` (all new opcodes since the last drain). If
531:     /// the producer produced multiple frames before this call they coalesce.
532:     pub fn frames(&mut self) -> Vec<Frame<'a>> {
533:         let frame_count = header::get_u32(self.header, OFF_FRAME_COUNT);
534:         if self.consumed >= frame_count {
535:             return Vec::new();
536:         }
537:         let mask = slot_mask(self.header);
538:         let start = ring_fn::cursor(self.header, OFF_READ_CURSOR, mask);
539:         let end = ring_fn::cursor(self.header, OFF_WRITE_CURSOR, mask);
540: 
541:         // The POC producer flushes before the ring fills, so `end >= start`
542:         // always holds. Guard against a wrapped ring by draining nothing; a
543:         // wrapped producer must flush first (see OPCODE.md backpressure).
544:         if end < start {
545:             return Vec::new();
546:         }
547: 
548:         // No new opcodes since the last drain (readCursor == writeCursor). This
549:         // also covers a freshly-created host view whose `consumed` counter
550:         // starts at 0 but whose cursors have already been drained by an earlier
551:         // view — without this, `next_frame` would return empty frames forever.
552:         if start == end {
553:             return Vec::new();
554:         }
555: 
556:         let frames = vec![Frame {
557:             slots: self.slots,
558:             arena: self.arena,
559:             start: start * Opcode::SIZE,
560:             end: end * Opcode::SIZE,
561:         }];
562: 
563:         header::set_u32(self.header, OFF_READ_CURSOR, end as u32);
564:         self.consumed = frame_count;
565: 
566:         // A `META::RESET` invalidates prior state: reset the host → guest event
567:         // arena cursor so the host starts bump-allocating fresh (matching the
568:         // guest arena's reset-on-RESET semantics).
569:         let reset_seen = self.slots[start * Opcode::SIZE..end * Opcode::SIZE]
570:             .chunks_exact(Opcode::SIZE)
571:             .any(|slot| {
572:                 let bytes: [u8; 16] = slot.try_into().unwrap();
573:                 let op = Opcode::from_bytes(&bytes);
574:                 op.category() == category::META && op.command() == crate::meta::RESET
575:             });
576:         if reset_seen {
577:             memory::header::set_u32(self.header, memory::OFF_EVENT_ARENA_CURSOR, 0);
578:         }
579: 
580:         frames
581:     }
582: 
583:     /// Write a raw-input event (host → guest) into the event ring, encoded as a
584:     /// 16-byte `EVENT` opcode. The renderer reports inputs here; the guest
585:     /// drains them via [`Guest::drain_events`].
586:     ///
587:     /// `TextChanged` text and `Navigate` URLs are bump-allocated into the
588:     /// host → guest **event arena** and referenced by their absolute offset in
589:     /// `B` (the `SET_TEXT` shared-memory convention); the guest resolves them
590:     /// from the same region. If the event arena is full the event is rejected
591:     /// with [`RingError::Full`] (backpressure).
592:     pub fn send_event(&mut self, event: &Event) -> Result<(), RingError> {
593:         let mask = slot_mask(self.header);
594:         let op = match event {
595:             Event::TextChanged { target, value } => {
596:                 let offset = crate::arena::alloc_event(&mut self.event_arena, self.header, value.as_bytes())
597:                     .map_err(|_| RingError::Full)?;
598:                 Opcode::new(category::EVENT, crate::event::TEXT_CHANGED, 0, *target, offset, 0)
599:             }
600:             Event::Navigate { url: Some(url) } => {
601:                 let offset = crate::arena::alloc_event(&mut self.event_arena, self.header, url.as_bytes())
602:                     .map_err(|_| RingError::Full)?;
603:                 Opcode::new(
604:                     category::EVENT,
605:                     crate::event::NAVIGATE,
606:                     crate::flag::NAVIGATE_URL,
607:                     0,
608:                     offset,
609:                     0,
610:                 )
611:             }
612:             _ => event.encode(),
613:         };
614:         ring_fn::push_event(self.event_slots, self.header, mask, &op)
615:     }
616: }

1: //! The fixed-size 16-byte Pathland opcode.
2: //!
3: //! Layout (see `spec/OPCODE.md`):
4: //!
5: //! ```text
6: //! [Category: u8][Command: u8][Flags: u16][A: u32][B: u32][C: u32]
7: //! ```
8: //!
9: //! All multi-byte fields are little-endian on the wire. `size_of::<Opcode>() == 16`,
10: //! so a 64-byte cache line holds exactly 4 opcodes.
11: 
12: use core::ptr;
13: 
14: /// Size of one opcode in bytes.
15: pub const OPCODE_SIZE: usize = 16;
16: 
17: /// A fixed-size 16-byte opcode.
18: ///
19: /// This struct intentionally mirrors the wire layout and is `#[repr(C, packed)]`
20: /// per the specification. Because it is packed, fields may be unaligned; always
21: /// read fields through the accessor methods (which use unaligned reads) rather
22: /// than by value.
23: #[repr(C, packed)]
24: #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
25: pub struct Opcode {
26:     /// Opcode category (see `constants::Category`).
27:     pub category: u8,
28:     /// Command within the category (see `constants::Command*`).
29:     pub command: u8,
30:     /// Category/command-specific flags.
31:     pub flags: u16,
32:     /// Primary payload.
33:     pub a: u32,
34:     /// Secondary payload.
35:     pub b: u32,
36:     /// Tertiary payload.
37:     pub c: u32,
38: }
39: 
40: impl Opcode {
41:     /// Byte size of an opcode (`16`).
42:     pub const SIZE: usize = OPCODE_SIZE;
43: 
44:     /// Construct an opcode from raw fields.
45:     #[inline]
46:     pub const fn new(category: u8, command: u8, flags: u16, a: u32, b: u32, c: u32) -> Self {
47:         Self {
48:             category,
49:             command,
50:             flags,
51:             a,
52:             b,
53:             c,
54:         }
55:     }
56: 
57:     /// The opcode category.
58:     #[inline]
59:     pub fn category(&self) -> u8 {
60:         self.category
61:     }
62: 
63:     /// The command within the category.
64:     #[inline]
65:     pub fn command(&self) -> u8 {
66:         self.command
67:     }
68: 
69:     /// The 16-bit flags word.
70:     #[inline]
71:     pub fn flags(&self) -> u16 {
72:         // SAFETY: read_unaligned is well-defined for packed fields.
73:         unsafe { ptr::addr_of!(self.flags).read_unaligned() }
74:     }
75: 
76:     /// Primary payload (little-endian u32).
77:     #[inline]
78:     pub fn a(&self) -> u32 {
79:         // SAFETY: read_unaligned is well-defined for packed fields.
80:         unsafe { ptr::addr_of!(self.a).read_unaligned() }
81:     }
82: 
83:     /// Secondary payload (little-endian u32).
84:     #[inline]
85:     pub fn b(&self) -> u32 {
86:         // SAFETY: read_unaligned is well-defined for packed fields.
87:         unsafe { ptr::addr_of!(self.b).read_unaligned() }
88:     }
89: 
90:     /// Tertiary payload (little-endian u32).
91:     #[inline]
92:     pub fn c(&self) -> u32 {
93:         // SAFETY: read_unaligned is well-defined for packed fields.
94:         unsafe { ptr::addr_of!(self.c).read_unaligned() }
95:     }
96: 
97:     /// Interpret `A` as an `f32` (bit-preserving).
98:     #[inline]
99:     pub fn a_f32(&self) -> f32 {
100:         f32::from_bits(self.a())
101:     }
102: 
103:     /// Interpret `B` as an `f32` (bit-preserving).
104:     #[inline]
105:     pub fn b_f32(&self) -> f32 {
106:         f32::from_bits(self.b())
107:     }
108: 
109:     /// Interpret `C` as an `f32` (bit-preserving).
110:     #[inline]
111:     pub fn c_f32(&self) -> f32 {
112:         f32::from_bits(self.c())
113:     }
114: 
115:     /// Serialize to the 16-byte wire representation (little-endian).
116:     pub fn to_bytes(&self) -> [u8; OPCODE_SIZE] {
117:         let mut out = [0u8; OPCODE_SIZE];
118:         out[0] = self.category;
119:         out[1] = self.command;
120:         // SAFETY: read_unaligned is well-defined for packed fields.
121:         let flags = unsafe { ptr::addr_of!(self.flags).read_unaligned() };
122:         let a = unsafe { ptr::addr_of!(self.a).read_unaligned() };
123:         let b = unsafe { ptr::addr_of!(self.b).read_unaligned() };
124:         let c = unsafe { ptr::addr_of!(self.c).read_unaligned() };
125:         out[2..4].copy_from_slice(&flags.to_le_bytes());
126:         out[4..8].copy_from_slice(&a.to_le_bytes());
127:         out[8..12].copy_from_slice(&b.to_le_bytes());
128:         out[12..16].copy_from_slice(&c.to_le_bytes());
129:         out
130:     }
131: 
132:     /// Deserialize from the 16-byte wire representation (little-endian).
133:     pub fn from_bytes(bytes: &[u8; OPCODE_SIZE]) -> Self {
134:         let category = bytes[0];
135:         let command = bytes[1];
136:         let flags = u16::from_le_bytes([bytes[2], bytes[3]]);
137:         let a = u32::from_le_bytes(bytes[4..8].try_into().unwrap());
138:         let b = u32::from_le_bytes(bytes[8..12].try_into().unwrap());
139:         let c = u32::from_le_bytes(bytes[12..16].try_into().unwrap());
140:         Self {
141:             category,
142:             command,
143:             flags,
144:             a,
145:             b,
146:             c,
147:         }
148:     }
149: }

175:         );

181:         let back = Opcode::from_bytes(&op.to_bytes());
182:         assert_eq!(back.a(), 42);
183:         assert_eq!(back.b_f32(), 100.0);
