1: //! Typed raw-input events (host → guest).
2: //!
3: //! Events are the **raw inputs** the renderer reports: pointer down/move/up and
4: //! key down/up, each carrying a host-resolved `targetId`. High-level
5: //! interpretations (tap, drag, long-press) are built by the guest/app from
6: //! these raw inputs and are NOT part of the protocol.
7: //!
8: //! Encode a raw input with `Event::encode`, decode a ring opcode with
9: //! `Event::try_from`.
10: 
11: use alloc::string::String;
12: use alloc::string::ToString;
13: use crate::category;
14: use crate::flag;
15: use crate::Opcode;
16: 
17: /// A raw-input event (host → guest).
18: ///
19: /// `Event` is **not** `Copy`: [`Event::TextChanged`] owns the new field text
20: /// and [`Event::Navigate`] owns an optional URL. Simple events round-trip
21: /// through `encode`/`try_from` as pure 16-byte opcodes; `TextChanged` and
22: /// `Navigate` with a URL are encoded/decoded at the batch level (their strings
23: /// live in the string section / event arena, referenced by a relative/absolute
24: /// offset).
25: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
26: pub enum Event {
27:     /// Pointer button pressed at a viewport-relative point.
28:     PointerDown {
29:         target: u32,
30:         x: f32,
31:         y: f32,
32:         secondary: bool,
33:     },
34:     /// Pointer moved; optionally entered/left the node (hover).
35:     PointerMove {
36:         target: u32,
37:         x: f32,
38:         y: f32,
39:         hovering: bool,
40:         leaving: bool,
41:     },
42:     /// Pointer button released at a viewport-relative point.
43:     PointerUp {
44:         target: u32,
45:         x: f32,
46:         y: f32,
47:         secondary: bool,
48:     },
49:     /// Key pressed (possibly an auto-repeat).
50:     KeyDown {
51:         target: u32,
52:         key_code: u16,
53:         modifiers: u8,
54:         repeat: bool,
55:     },
56:     /// Key released.
57:     KeyUp {
58:         target: u32,
59:         key_code: u16,
60:         modifiers: u8,
61:     },
62:     /// A control's value changed (host → guest). The renderer resolves the
63:     /// semantic value (e.g. a slider thumb dragged along its track) and reports
64:     /// it here; the guest/app writes it into its bound state.
65:     ValueChanged {
66:         target: u32,
67:         value: f32,
68:     },
69:     /// A text field's value changed (host → guest). The new text is resolved
70:     /// from the batch's string section (see the doc comment on this enum).
71:     TextChanged {
72:         target: u32,
73:         value: String,
74:     },
75:     /// A node gained/lost focus (host → guest). Draft command 0x08.
76:     FocusChanged { target: u32, focused: bool },
77:     /// An editing session began/ended (host → guest). Draft command 0x09.
78:     EditingChanged { target: u32, editing: bool },
79:     /// The user committed a field (host → guest). Draft command 0x0A.
80:     Submit { target: u32 },
81:     /// A scroll container's offset changed (host → guest). Draft command 0x0B.
82:     Scroll {
83:         target: u32,
84:         offset_x: f32,
85:         offset_y: f32,
86:     },
87:     /// Raw wheel/trackpad deltas (host → guest). Draft command 0x0C.
88:     Wheel {
89:         target: u32,
90:         delta_x: f32,
91:         delta_y: f32,
92:     },
93:     /// A `DATE_PICKER`'s value changed (host → guest). Draft command 0x0D;
94:     /// `days` is I32 (pre-1970 negative), `millis` is millis of day.
95:     DateChanged {
96:         target: u32,
97:         days: i32,
98:         millis: u32,
99:     },
100:     /// A global navigation request (host → guest). Draft command 0x0E; never
101:     /// node-keyed. `url: Some(...)` carries the destination URL the platform
102:     /// navigated to (browser `popstate`/back/forward/deep-link), resolved from
103:     /// the string section / event arena; `url: None` is a native back request.
104:     Navigate { url: Option<String> },
105: }

107: impl Event {
108:     /// Encode this event as a 16-byte opcode.
109:     ///
110:     /// `TextChanged` and `Navigate` with a URL cannot be fully encoded here —
111:     /// their strings live in the batch's string section / event arena — so this
112:     /// emits the opcode with a zero `B` offset; the batch-aware
113:     /// `encode_events`/`decode_events` pair in `pathland-core-transport` writes
114:     /// the string and its real offset.
115:     pub fn encode(&self) -> Opcode {
116:         match self {
117:             Event::PointerDown {
118:                 target,
119:                 x,
120:                 y,
121:                 secondary,
122:             } => Opcode::new(
123:                 category::EVENT,
124:                 crate::event::POINTER_DOWN,
125:                 flag_for(*secondary, false, false),
126:                 *target,
127:                 x.to_bits(),
128:                 y.to_bits(),
129:             ),
130:             Event::PointerMove {
131:                 target,
132:                 x,
133:                 y,
134:                 hovering,
135:                 leaving,
136:             } => Opcode::new(
137:                 category::EVENT,
138:                 crate::event::POINTER_MOVE,
139:                 flag_for(false, *hovering, *leaving),
140:                 *target,
141:                 x.to_bits(),
142:                 y.to_bits(),
143:             ),
144:             Event::PointerUp {
145:                 target,
146:                 x,
147:                 y,
148:                 secondary,
149:             } => Opcode::new(
150:                 category::EVENT,
151:                 crate::event::POINTER_UP,
152:                 flag_for(*secondary, false, false),
153:                 *target,
154:                 x.to_bits(),
155:                 y.to_bits(),
156:             ),
157:             Event::KeyDown {
158:                 target,
159:                 key_code,
160:                 modifiers,
161:                 repeat,
162:             } => Opcode::new(
163:                 category::EVENT,
164:                 crate::event::KEY_DOWN,
165:                 if *repeat { flag::KEY_REPEAT } else { 0 },
166:                 *target,
167:                 *key_code as u32,
168:                 *modifiers as u32,
169:             ),
170:             Event::KeyUp {
171:                 target,
172:                 key_code,
173:                 modifiers,
174:             } => Opcode::new(
175:                 category::EVENT,
176:                 crate::event::KEY_UP,
177:                 0,
178:                 *target,
179:                 *key_code as u32,
180:                 *modifiers as u32,
181:             ),
182:             Event::ValueChanged { target, value } => Opcode::new(
183:                 category::EVENT,
184:                 crate::event::VALUE_CHANGED,
185:                 0,
186:                 *target,
187:                 value.to_bits(),
188:                 0,
189:             ),
190:             Event::TextChanged { target, .. } => Opcode::new(
191:                 category::EVENT,
192:                 crate::event::TEXT_CHANGED,
193:                 0,
194:                 *target,
195:                 0,
196:                 0,
197:             ),
198:             Event::FocusChanged { target, focused } => Opcode::new(
199:                 category::EVENT,
200:                 crate::event::FOCUS_CHANGED,
201:                 0,
202:                 *target,
203:                 u32::from(*focused),
204:                 0,
205:             ),
206:             Event::EditingChanged { target, editing } => Opcode::new(
207:                 category::EVENT,
208:                 crate::event::EDITING_CHANGED,
209:                 0,
210:                 *target,
211:                 u32::from(*editing),
212:                 0,
213:             ),
214:             Event::Submit { target } => Opcode::new(
215:                 category::EVENT,
216:                 crate::event::SUBMIT,
217:                 0,
218:                 *target,
219:                 0,
220:                 0,
221:             ),
222:             Event::Scroll {
223:                 target,
224:                 offset_x,
225:                 offset_y,
226:             } => Opcode::new(
227:                 category::EVENT,
228:                 crate::event::SCROLL,
229:                 0,
230:                 *target,
231:                 offset_x.to_bits(),
232:                 offset_y.to_bits(),
233:             ),
234:             Event::Wheel {
235:                 target,
236:                 delta_x,
237:                 delta_y,
238:             } => Opcode::new(
239:                 category::EVENT,
240:                 crate::event::WHEEL,
241:                 0,
242:                 *target,
243:                 delta_x.to_bits(),
244:                 delta_y.to_bits(),
245:             ),
246:             Event::DateChanged {
247:                 target,
248:                 days,
249:                 millis,
250:             } => Opcode::new(
251:                 category::EVENT,
252:                 crate::event::DATE_CHANGED,
253:                 0,
254:                 *target,
255:                 *days as u32,
256:                 *millis,
257:             ),
258:             Event::Navigate { url } => Opcode::new(
259:                 category::EVENT,
260:                 crate::event::NAVIGATE,
261:                 if url.is_some() { flag::NAVIGATE_URL } else { 0 },
262:                 0,
263:                 0,
264:                 0,
265:             ),
266:         }
267:     }
268: }

270: /// Build a pointer-opcode flags word from the pointer/hover bits.
271: #[inline]
272: fn flag_for(secondary: bool, hovering: bool, leaving: bool) -> u16 {
273:     let mut flags = 0u16;
274:     if secondary {
275:         flags |= flag::POINTER_SECONDARY;
276:     }
277:     if hovering {
278:         flags |= flag::HOVER_ENTER;
279:     }
280:     if leaving {
281:         flags |= flag::HOVER_LEAVE;
282:     }
283:     flags
284: }
285: 
286: /// Error decoding a raw-input event from an opcode.
287: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
288: pub enum EventError {
289:     /// The opcode is not an `EVENT` category opcode.
290:     NotAnEvent,
291:     /// The opcode is an EVENT category opcode but an unknown command.
292:     UnknownCommand,
293:     /// The opcode is `TEXT_CHANGED`, which needs the batch's string section to
294:     /// resolve its text; decode it with `pathland-core-transport::decode_events`
295:     /// instead of a bare opcode.
296:     NeedsStringSection,
297: }
298: 
299: impl TryFrom<Opcode> for Event {
300:     type Error = EventError;
301: 
302:     fn try_from(op: Opcode) -> Result<Self, Self::Error> {
303:         if op.category() != category::EVENT {
304:             return Err(EventError::NotAnEvent);
305:         }
306:         let flags = op.flags();
307:         match op.command() {
308:             crate::event::POINTER_DOWN => Ok(Event::PointerDown {
309:                 target: op.a(),
310:                 x: op.b_f32(),
311:                 y: op.c_f32(),
312:                 secondary: flags & flag::POINTER_SECONDARY != 0,
313:             }),
314:             crate::event::POINTER_MOVE => Ok(Event::PointerMove {
315:                 target: op.a(),
316:                 x: op.b_f32(),
317:                 y: op.c_f32(),
318:                 hovering: flags & flag::HOVER_ENTER != 0,
319:                 leaving: flags & flag::HOVER_LEAVE != 0,
320:             }),
321:             crate::event::POINTER_UP => Ok(Event::PointerUp {
322:                 target: op.a(),
323:                 x: op.b_f32(),
324:                 y: op.c_f32(),
325:                 secondary: flags & flag::POINTER_SECONDARY != 0,
326:             }),
327:             crate::event::KEY_DOWN => Ok(Event::KeyDown {
328:                 target: op.a(),
329:                 key_code: op.b() as u16,
330:                 modifiers: op.c() as u8,
331:                 repeat: flags & flag::KEY_REPEAT != 0,
332:             }),
333:             crate::event::KEY_UP => Ok(Event::KeyUp {
334:                 target: op.a(),
335:                 key_code: op.b() as u16,
336:                 modifiers: op.c() as u8,
337:             }),
338:             crate::event::VALUE_CHANGED => Ok(Event::ValueChanged {
339:                 target: op.a(),
340:                 value: op.b_f32(),
341:             }),
342:             crate::event::FOCUS_CHANGED => Ok(Event::FocusChanged {
343:                 target: op.a(),
344:                 focused: op.b() != 0,
345:             }),
346:             crate::event::EDITING_CHANGED => Ok(Event::EditingChanged {
347:                 target: op.a(),
348:                 editing: op.b() != 0,
349:             }),
350:             crate::event::SUBMIT => Ok(Event::Submit { target: op.a() }),
351:             crate::event::SCROLL => Ok(Event::Scroll {
352:                 target: op.a(),
353:                 offset_x: op.b_f32(),
354:                 offset_y: op.c_f32(),
355:             }),
356:             crate::event::WHEEL => Ok(Event::Wheel {
357:                 target: op.a(),
358:                 delta_x: op.b_f32(),

379: /// Decode an event opcode for the **shared-memory path**, resolving
380: /// `TEXT_CHANGED` text and `NAVIGATE` URLs from the host → guest event arena
381: /// (`B` is an absolute offset into that region). Non-string events decode as
382: /// usual.
383: ///
384: /// Returns `None` for non-event opcodes, unknown commands, or string events
385: /// whose offset cannot be resolved (invalid or out of range).
386: pub fn decode_event(op: &Opcode, event_arena: &[u8]) -> Option<Event> {
387:     if op.category() != category::EVENT {
388:         return None;
389:     }
390:     if op.command() == crate::event::TEXT_CHANGED {
391:         let text = crate::arena::get_str(event_arena, op.b()).ok()?;
392:         return Some(Event::TextChanged {
393:             target: op.a(),
394:             value: text.to_string(),
395:         });
396:     }
397:     if op.command() == crate::event::NAVIGATE && op.flags() & flag::NAVIGATE_URL != 0 {
398:         let url = crate::arena::get_str(event_arena, op.b()).ok()?;
399:         return Some(Event::Navigate {
400:             url: Some(url.to_string()),
401:         });
402:     }
403:     Event::try_from(*op).ok()
404: }

16: /// consumers are granted short-lived `Guest`/`Host` views over the same buffer
17: /// via the borrowed methods, so opcodes flow in place with no copies.
18: #[derive(Debug)]
19: pub struct RingTransport {
20:     /// Shared linear memory (header | ring | arena).
21:     mem: Vec<u8>,
22:     /// Ring/arena geometry.
23:     layout: MemoryLayout,
24: }
25: 
26: impl RingTransport {
27:     /// Create a ring transport with a default layout and a zeroed header.
28:     pub fn new() -> Self {
29:         let layout = MemoryLayout::default();
30:         let mut mem = vec![0u8; layout.total_bytes()];
31:         init_memory(&mut mem, &layout);
32:         Self { mem, layout }
33:     }
34: 
35:     /// Create a ring transport over a caller-provided buffer/layout.
36:     pub fn with_buffer(mem: Vec<u8>, layout: MemoryLayout) -> Self {
37:         Self { mem, layout }
38:     }
39: 
40:     /// The memory layout (region geometry).
41:     pub fn layout(&self) -> &MemoryLayout {
42:         &self.layout
43:     }
44: 
45:     /// Create a producer view over the shared buffer (writes opcodes + arena).
46:     ///
47:     /// Drop the returned `Guest` before calling `next_frame`; producer and
48:     /// consumer must not overlap borrows.
49:     pub fn producer(&mut self) -> Guest<'_> {
50:         Guest::new(&mut self.mem, &self.layout)
51:     }
52: 
53:     /// Peak at the raw underlying buffer (for embedding/custom transports).
54:     pub fn buffer(&self) -> &[u8] {
55:         &self.mem
56:     }
57: }
58: 
59: impl Default for RingTransport {
60:     fn default() -> Self {
61:         Self::new()
62:     }
63: }
64: 
65: impl FrameSource for RingTransport {
66:     fn next_frame(&mut self) -> Result<Option<OpcodeBatch<'_>>, TransportError> {
67:         let mut host = Host::new(&mut self.mem, &self.layout);
68:         let mut frames = host.frames();
69:         match frames.pop() {
70:             Some(frame) => Ok(Some(OpcodeBatch::new(
71:                 frame,
72:                 crate::direction::GUEST_TO_HOST,
73:             ))),
74:             None => Ok(None),
75:         }
76:     }
77: }
78: 
79: impl DriverTransport for RingTransport {
80:     fn send_input(&mut self, event: &pathland_core::Event) -> Result<(), TransportError> {
81:         // The host writes the raw input as an EVENT-category opcode into the
82:         // host → guest event ring; the guest drains it via `drain_events`.
83:         let mut host = Host::new(&mut self.mem, &self.layout);
84:         host.send_event(event).map_err(|_| {
85:             TransportError::Protocol(crate::ProtocolError::BadInput)
86:         })
87:     }
88: }
89: 
90: impl RingTransport {
91:     /// Drain raw-input events written by the host into the host → guest event
92:     /// ring, decoding each `EVENT` opcode (guest side).
93:     pub fn drain_events(&mut self) -> Vec<pathland_core::Event> {
94:         let mut guest = self.producer();
95:         guest.drain_events()
96:     }
97: }

178:     fn next_frame_is_zero_copy() {
179:         // The ring is a single shared linear-memory buffer. Reading a frame
180:         // must borrow that buffer in place — never copy the opcode stream.
181:         // Prove two things:
182:         //  1. Reading N opcodes allocates O(1) bookkeeping, not O(N) storage
183:         //     (a copy of the opcode stream would allocate per-opcode).
184:         //  2. The arena string decoded from the frame lives inside the shared

195:         unsafe impl GlobalAlloc for Counting {
196:             unsafe fn alloc(&self, l: AllocLayout) -> *mut u8 {

216:         let arena_ref = {

223:             guest.end_frame();

228:         // borrowed, so allocations must be O(1), independent of the opcode count.
229:         COUNT.with(|c| c.set(0));
230:         let batch = ring.next_frame().unwrap().expect("a frame");
231:         let frame = batch.frame();
232: 
233:         let decoded: usize = frame.opcodes().count();
234:         let arena = frame.arena_str(arena_ref).expect("arena string");
235: 
236:         let allocs = COUNT.with(|c| c.get());

238:         assert_eq!(decoded, OPCODES + 1, "create_node + set_text");
239:         assert_eq!(arena, "zero-copy proof");
240: 
241:         // The arena string is read in place from the shared buffer.
242:         let str_ptr = arena.as_ptr() as usize;
243:         assert!(
244:             str_ptr >= buf_base && str_ptr < buf_end,
245:             "arena string must be borrowed from the shared ring (ptr {str_ptr:#x} outside {buf_base:#x}..{buf_end:#x})"
246:         );
247: 
248:         // No per-opcode copying: a handful of O(1) bookkeeping allocations is
249:         // fine; anything O(opcodes) would mean the opcode stream was copied.
250:         assert!(
251:             allocs < OPCODES,
252:             "reading {OPCODES} opcodes must not copy them (allocations: {allocs})"

1: //! Transport abstraction: how opcode batches move from producer to consumer.
2: //!
3: //! The UI runtime produces renderer-neutral opcodes and knows nothing about the
4: //! transport. This module defines the boundary between:
5: //!
6: //! - the **producer** (opcode engine) that emits opcodes, and
7: //! - the **consumer** (driver) that reads them.
8: //!
9: //! Local transports (shared-memory ring) may be zero-copy; remote transports
10: //! (WebSocket/IPC) copy and serialize. Both conform to the same traits.
11: //!
12: //! The two ends are deliberately separate because a transport is often split
13: //! across a process/IPC boundary, with different backpressure and blocking
14: //! semantics on each side.
15: 
16: use pathland_core::Frame;
17: 
18: /// A single in-memory transport unit: one frame of opcodes + arena plus
19: /// transport metadata. Distinct from the raw opcode stream and from the
20: /// wire-format batch.
21: pub struct OpcodeBatch<'a> {
22:     frame: Frame<'a>,
23:     /// Transport direction bitmask (see [`crate::direction`]).
24:     direction: u16,
25: }
26: 
27: impl<'a> OpcodeBatch<'a> {
28:     /// Wrap a frame as a transport batch (guest → host by default).
29:     pub fn new(frame: Frame<'a>, direction: u16) -> Self {
30:         Self { frame, direction }
31:     }
32: 
33:     /// The frame carried by this batch.
34:     pub fn frame(&self) -> &Frame<'a> {
35:         &self.frame
36:     }
37: 
38:     /// Transport direction bitmask.
39:     pub fn direction(&self) -> u16 {
40:         self.direction
41:     }
42: }
43: 
44: /// Errors produced by a transport while sending or receiving.
45: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
46: pub enum TransportError {
47:     /// The consumer has not drained; the producer should retain and retry.
48:     Backpressure,
49:     /// The transport is closed/terminated.
50:     Closed,
51:     /// The peer violated the protocol.
52:     Protocol(ProtocolError),
53: }
54: 
55: /// Sub-errors for protocol violations.
56: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
57: pub enum ProtocolError {
58:     /// The remote sent a version this side does not support.
59:     BadVersion,
60:     /// The payload is malformed (bad magic, truncated, bad length).
61:     Malformed,
62:     /// A raw input could not be interpreted.
63:     BadInput,
64: }
65: 
66: /// Handles raw-input events arriving from the host (renderer → engine).
67: ///
68: /// The driver resolves a raw input to a node id (via hit-testing) and dispatches
69: /// it here; the transport's guest side forwards it to the guest engine.
70: pub trait InputSink {
71:     /// Deliver a raw input (host → guest).
72:     fn dispatch(&mut self, event: &pathland_core::Event);
73: }
74: 
75: /// The consumer side of a transport: the driver reads frames here.
76: ///
77: /// A transport may be blocking or non-blocking; `next_frame` reflects that.
78: /// The returned `Frame` borrows the transport's backing memory (zero-copy when
79: /// possible); consume it before the next call.
80: pub trait FrameSource {
81:     /// Read the next available frame, or `None` if none is ready.
82:     ///
83:     /// Blocking vs non-blocking semantics are transport-specific (documented
84:     /// per implementation).
85:     fn next_frame(&mut self) -> Result<Option<OpcodeBatch<'_>>, TransportError>;
86: }
87: 
88: /// A consumer-side transport that can also send raw inputs back to the guest.
89: pub trait DriverTransport: FrameSource {
90:     /// Send a raw input from the host to the guest over this transport.
91:     fn send_input(&mut self, event: &pathland_core::Event) -> Result<(), TransportError>;
92: }

1: package com.pathland.demo.gtk;
2: 
3: import com.pathland.view.Commands;
4: import com.pathland.view.transport.Event;
5: import com.sun.jna.Pointer;
6: 
7: import java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets;
8: import java.util.ArrayList;
9: import java.util.List;
10: 
11: /**
12:  * Decodes raw {@code EVENT}-category opcodes drained from the shared ring
13:  * ({@code pathland_core_drain_events}) into {@link Event} objects, resolving
14:  * strings ({@code TEXT_CHANGED}, {@code NAVIGATE} URLs) from the shared
15:  * host → guest event arena. The wire is the opcode engine — never a
16:  * side-channel callback.
17:  */
18: public final class RingEventReader {
19: 
20:     private static final int OPCODE_SIZE = 16;
21:     private static final int CATEGORY_EVENT = 0x03;
22: 
23:     /** Ring header: byte offset of the event-arena offset (spec/OPCODE.md, memory.rs). */
24:     private static final int OFF_EVENT_ARENA_OFFSET = 0x40;
25: 
26:     private final Pointer ringPtr;
27:     private final long ringLen;
28:     private final int eventArenaOffset;
29: 
30:     public RingEventReader(Pointer ringPtr, long ringLen) {
31:         this.ringPtr = ringPtr;
32:         this.ringLen = ringLen;
33:         if (ringPtr != null && ringLen >= OFF_EVENT_ARENA_OFFSET + 4L) {
34:             this.eventArenaOffset = ringPtr.getInt(OFF_EVENT_ARENA_OFFSET);
35:         } else {
36:             this.eventArenaOffset = 0;
37:         }
38:     }
39: 
40:     /** Decode consecutive 16-byte opcodes from {@code raw} (a drain buffer). */
41:     public List<Event> decode(byte[] raw) {
42:         List<Event> events = new ArrayList<>();
43:         for (int off = 0; off + OPCODE_SIZE <= raw.length; off += OPCODE_SIZE) {
44:             if ((raw[off] & 0xFF) != CATEGORY_EVENT) {
45:                 continue;
46:             }
47:             int command = raw[off + 1] & 0xFF;
48:             int flags = u16(raw, off + 2);
49:             int a = i32(raw, off + 4);
50:             int b = i32(raw, off + 8);
51:             int c = i32(raw, off + 12);
52:             Event event = decodeOne(command, flags, a, b, c);
53:             if (event != null) {
54:                 events.add(event);
55:             }
56:         }
57:         return events;
58:     }
59: 
60:     private Event decodeOne(int command, int flags, int a, int b, int c) {
61:         return switch (command) {
62:             case Commands.Event.POINTER_DOWN -> Event.pointerDown(a, f32(b), f32(c));
63:             case Commands.Event.POINTER_UP -> Event.pointerUp(a, f32(b), f32(c));
64:             case Commands.Event.POINTER_MOVE -> Event.pointerMove(a, f32(b), f32(c), flags);
65:             case Commands.Event.KEY_DOWN -> Event.keyDown(a, b, c, flags);
66:             case Commands.Event.KEY_UP -> Event.keyUp(a, b, c);
67:             case Commands.Event.VALUE_CHANGED -> Event.valueChanged(a, f32(b));
68:             case Commands.Event.TEXT_CHANGED -> Event.textChanged(a, arenaString(b));
69:             case Commands.Event.FOCUS_CHANGED -> Event.focusChanged(a, b != 0);
70:             case Commands.Event.EDITING_CHANGED -> Event.editingChanged(a, b != 0);
71:             case Commands.Event.SUBMIT -> Event.submit(a);
72:             case Commands.Event.SCROLL -> Event.scroll(a, f32(b), f32(c));
73:             case Commands.Event.WHEEL -> Event.wheel(a, f32(b), f32(c));
74:             case Commands.Event.DATE_CHANGED -> Event.dateChanged(a, b, c);
75:             case Commands.Event.NAVIGATE -> (flags & Commands.Flags.NAVIGATE_URL) != 0
76:                     ? Event.navigate(arenaString(b))
77:                     : Event.navigateBack();
78:             default -> null;
79:         };
80:     }
81: 
82:     /** Resolve a string from the shared event arena at {@code ref} ([u32 len][bytes]). */
83:     private String arenaString(int ref) {
84:         if (ref < 0 || ringPtr == null || eventArenaOffset <= 0) {
85:             return null;
86:         }
87:         long base = (long) eventArenaOffset + ref;
88:         if (base + 4 > ringLen) {
89:             return null;
90:         }
91:         int len = ringPtr.getInt(base);
92:         if (len < 0 || base + 4 + len > ringLen) {
93:             return null;
94:         }
95:         byte[] bytes = ringPtr.getByteArray(base + 4, len);
96:         return new String(bytes, StandardCharsets.UTF_8);
97:     }
98: 
99:     private static int u16(byte[] raw, int off) {
100:         return (raw[off] & 0xFF) | ((raw[off + 1] & 0xFF) << 8);
101:     }
102: 
103:     private static int i32(byte[] raw, int off) {
104:         return (raw[off] & 0xFF) | ((raw[off + 1] & 0xFF) << 8)
105:                 | ((raw[off + 2] & 0xFF) << 16) | ((raw[off + 3] & 0xFF) << 24);
106:     }
107: 
108:     private static float f32(int bits) {
109:         return Float.intBitsToFloat(bits);
110:     }
111: }

1: # Pathland Opcode Protocol Specification
2: 
3: **Wire protocol version:** 1
4: **Status:** Draft
5: **Format:** Fixed-size (16-byte) opcode engine
6: **Last Updated:** September 3, 2026
7: 
8: ---
9: 
10: ## Overview
11: 
12: The Pathland Opcode Protocol is the **fixed-size instruction engine** at the heart of the Rust-first architecture. The **opcode engine** emits the application's **declarative view structure** — VStack, HStack, Text, spacing, padding, alignment — as a stream of fixed 16-byte opcodes into a **ring buffer** in **linear memory**. The host renderer consumes the ring and maps the structure onto that platform's **native elements** (GTK4 widgets, DOM elements, HTML).
13: 
14: **The engine does not compute layout and does not emit rects.** Native renderers lay out their own native elements from the constraint properties the engine passes through. This is the Pathland principle: *always render through that platform's native elements.*
15: 
16: This specification supersedes the historical variable-length binary instruction format (which has been removed from the repository).
17: 
18: ### Goals
19: 
20: - **Sub-millisecond execution**: every opcode is a fixed 16 bytes; emission is a diff over the retained tree with **zero dynamic heap allocations** in the steady state.
21: - **L1 CPU cache alignment**: a 64-byte cache line holds exactly **4 opcodes**. Ring slots are 16-byte aligned and densely packed.
22: - **Reactive emission**: only the nodes that changed emit opcodes. An unchanged tree emits **zero** opcodes (see [Reactive Emission](#reactive-emission)).
23: - **Linear, deterministic decoding**: the host walks the ring with a single cursor.
24: 
25: ### Core Principles
26: 
27: 1. **Fixed-size instructions**: every opcode is exactly 16 bytes — no length prefixes, no skippable-variable framing.
28: 2. **Declarative, not positioned**: the engine describes *what* the UI is (stacks, text, constraints), never *where* it is. Native elements compute their own positions.
29: 3. **Numeric IDs**: categories, commands, component types, and properties are numeric.
30: 4. **Native elements**: renderers map the opcode stream onto that platform's native elements — never a generic canvas unless a platform has no native equivalent.
31: 5. **Zero-copy**: the ring and arena are plain regions of the same linear memory shared with the host.
32: 6. **Single-producer / single-consumer**: the guest engine produces; the host renderer consumes. No locks required.
33: 
34: ---
35: 
36: ## Opcode Format
37: 
38: Every opcode is exactly **16 bytes**:
39: 
40: ```
41: [Category: u8][Command: u8][Flags: u16][A: u32][B: u32][C: u32]
42: ```
43: 
44: | Field | Size | Offset | Description |
45: |-------|------|--------|-------------|
46: | `Category` | 1B | 0 | Opcode category (see [Category Table](#category-table)) |
47: | `Command` | 1B | 1 | Command within the category (see [Command Tables](#command-tables)) |
48: | `Flags` | 2B | 2 | Category/command-specific flags |
49: | `A` | 4B | 4 | Primary payload |
50: | `B` | 4B | 8 | Secondary payload |
51: | `C` | 4B | 12 | Tertiary payload |
52: 
53: All multi-byte values are **little-endian**. The Rust reference type is `#[repr(C, packed)]`:
54: 
55: ```rust
56: #[repr(C, packed)]
57: pub struct Opcode {
58:     pub category: u8,
59:     pub command: u8,
60:     pub flags: u16,
61:     pub a: u32,
62:     pub b: u32,
63:     pub c: u32,
64: }
65: ```
66: 
67: `size_of::<Opcode>() == 16`.
68: 
69: ### Payload encoding conventions
70: 
71: - **Float payloads** (`spacing`, `padding`, sizes) are stored as raw `f32` (IEEE 754) bit patterns in a `u32` field.
72: - **Signed payloads** (the `I32` value type, and dedicated commands like `SET_DATE`'s days-since-epoch) are stored as the raw two's-complement bit pattern of a signed value in a `u32` field; a consumer reinterprets the field as `i32`.
73: - **Node IDs** are `u32`.
74: - **Component types / property IDs** are `u16`; when packed into a 4-byte payload they occupy the low two bytes (the high bytes are reserved / zero unless documented).
75: - **Arena references** are a `u32` byte offset into the arena region (see [Arena](#arena)).
76: - **Colors** are packed `0xAARRGGBB` in sRGB (see [Colors](#colors)).
77: 
78: ### Reserved ranges
79: 
80: - `Category == 0` is reserved (invalid).
81: - `Command == 0` in any category is reserved (invalid).
82: - `Category 0x80-0xFF`: custom/extended categories.
83: 
84: ---
85: 
86: ## Category Table
87: 
88: | Category | Value | Name | Producer | Description |
89: |----------|-------|------|----------|-------------|
90: | `TREE` | `0x01` | Tree mutations | Guest engine | Node create/delete/insert/remove/move |
91: | `STYLE` | `0x02` | Constraints & tokens | Guest engine | Property values (spacing, padding, …), design tokens |
92: | `EVENT` | `0x03` | Raw inputs | Host renderer | Pointer down/move/up, key down/up |
93: | `META` | `0x04` | Control | Both | Reset, environment |
94: 
95: ---
96: 
97: ## Command Tables
98: 
99: ### TREE (0x01)
100: 
101: The `componentType` values (the primitive views the protocol supports) are
102: catalogued in [PRIMITIVES.md](./PRIMITIVES.md), grouped by their SwiftUI
103: counterpart. Component IDs are allocated there spec-first; this file remains
104: the wire-format authority.
105: 
106: | Command | Value | A | B | C | Flags | Description |
107: |---------|-------|---|---|---|-------|-------------|
108: | `CREATE_NODE` | `0x01` | nodeId | componentType (u16, low) | 0 | — | Create a node of `componentType` |
109: | `DELETE_NODE` | `0x02` | nodeId | 0 | 0 | — | Delete a node and its subtree |
110: | `INSERT_CHILD` | `0x03` | parentId | childId | index | — | Insert `childId` into `parentId` at `index`; append is `index = u32::MAX` (`APPEND`) |
111: | `REMOVE_CHILD` | `0x04` | parentId | childId | 0 | — | Remove `childId` from `parentId` |
112: | `MOVE_CHILD` | `0x05` | parentId | childId | newIndex | — | Move child to `newIndex` (after removal); append is `newIndex = u32::MAX` (`APPEND`) |

114: ### STYLE (0x02)
115: 
116: The engine does not emit positions. `STYLE` carries the **constraint properties**
117: that native renderers feed to their own layout — spacing, alignment, FILL/HUG
118: size hints — plus **styling modifiers** (padding, colors, fonts, borders).
119: 
120: | Command | Value | A | B | C | Flags | Description |
121: |---------|-------|---|---|---|-------|-------------|
122: | `SET_PROPERTY` | `0x01` | nodeId | propertyId (u16, low) + valueType (u8, high byte) | value | — | Set a constraint/style property; `value` depends on `valueType` |
123: | `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` | `0x02` | arenaRef (path) | valueType (u8) | value | — | Override a design token; path is an arena string |
124: | `SET_TEXT` | `0x03` | nodeId | arenaRef (utf8) | 0 | — | Set a node's text content |
125: | `SET_DATE` | `0x04` | nodeId | days since epoch (I32) | millis of day (U32) | — | Set a node's date value (e.g. a `DATE_PICKER`); see [EVENTS.md](./EVENTS.md#date) for the matching `DATE_CHANGED` event |
126: 
127: `SET_PROPERTY` encodes the value type in the **high byte of `B`** (bits 24–31) and the property id in the low two bytes:
128: 
129: ```
130: B = (valueType << 16) | propertyId
131: ```
132: 
133: #### Value types
134: 
135: | Value Type | Value | C / value encoding |
136: |------------|-------|--------------------|
137: | `U8` | `0x01` | low byte of C |
138: | `U32` | `0x02` | u32 |
139: | `I32` | `0x03` | i32 |
140: | `F32` | `0x04` | f32 |
141: | `STRING` | `0x05` | arenaRef (utf8) |
142: | `ENUM` | `0x06` | low byte of C |
143: | `COLOR` | `0x07` | packed `0xAARRGGBB` |
144: | `DESIGN_TOKEN` | `0x08` | arenaRef (token path) |
145: 
146: > **Enum-valued properties** (`ALIGNMENT`, `TEXT_ALIGNMENT`, `TRUNCATION_MODE`,
147: > `ROLE`, `STATE`, and the draft `FONT_*`/`CONTENT_MODE`/`CONTROL_SIZE`/`SHAPE_KIND`
148: > properties) are carried with the **`F32` value type**, holding the numeric enum
149: > code as an f32 bit pattern (e.g. `ALIGNMENT=Center(1)` → `C = 1.0f32.to_bits()`).
150: > The enumerated code tables live in
151: > [MODIFIERS.md](./MODIFIERS.md#appendix-enumerated-values). The `ENUM` value type
152: > (low byte of `C`) is available for explicitly `ENUM`-coded properties.
153: >
154: > **Token references**: any property that normally carries a `COLOR` / `F32` /
155: > `STRING` / `ENUM` value MAY instead carry the `DESIGN_TOKEN` value type, with
156: > `C` = arenaRef to a token path (see [Design Token System](#design-token-system)
157: > and [TOKENS.md](./TOKENS.md)).

159: #### Constraint properties for native layout
160: 
161: The following properties drive native layout; the renderer maps them to its
162: native equivalents (e.g. `SPACING` → GTK box spacing / CSS `gap`, `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT`
163: → size requests). Special `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` values: `-1` = FILL (expand to
164: available), `-2` = HUG_CONTENT (native intrinsic size).

167: |----------|-------|------|----------------|

170: | `CONTENT_MARGINS` | `0x0005` | F32 | Uniform inset between a stack's edge and its content |
171: | `WIDTH` | `0x100B` | F32 | Width hint (-1 FILL, -2 HUG) |
172: | `HEIGHT` | `0x100C` | F32 | Height hint (-1 FILL, -2 HUG) |

197: |----------|-------|------|----------------|

305: ### EVENT (0x03) — host → guest
306: 
307: The event commands and their `EVENT_LISTENERS` bits are catalogued in
308: [EVENTS.md](./EVENTS.md) (core events, SwiftUI-style); this file defines the
309: wire encoding.
310: 
311: Events are the **raw inputs**: the renderer reports what happened (a pointer
312: went down/moved/up, a key went down/up) and resolves which node it hit via its
313: own rendered-output tree. High-level interpretations — tap, drag, long-press —
314: are built by the guest/app from these raw inputs and are **not** part of the
315: protocol.
316: 
317: #### Event listeners (which nodes emit events)
318: 
319: A renderer reports raw events only for nodes that declared they want them. The
320: application declares this intent through the `EVENT_LISTENERS` semantic
321: property (`0x2005`, a u32 bitmask, `SET_PROPERTY` with the `U32` value type).
322: Each bit requests a raw-input event kind (see [`listener`] flags):
323: 
324: | Bit | Mask | Event command | Meaning |
325: |-----|------|---------------|---------|
326: | 0 | `0x00000001` | `POINTER_DOWN` | Report pointer-down for this node |
327: | 1 | `0x00000002` | `POINTER_MOVE` | Report pointer-move/enter/leave |
328: | 2 | `0x00000004` | `POINTER_UP` | Report pointer-up for this node |
329: | 3 | `0x00000008` | `KEY_DOWN` | Report key-down |
330: | 4 | `0x00000010` | `KEY_UP` | Report key-up |
331: 
332: > Bits 5–9 (draft) are allocated in [EVENTS.md](./EVENTS.md#event-listeners-event_listeners)
333: > for `FOCUS_CHANGED`, `EDITING_CHANGED`, `SUBMIT`, `SCROLL`, and `WHEEL`.
334: > Value-bearing controls (`SLIDER`, `TOGGLE`, `DATE_PICKER`, …) report their
335: > value changes by component type and do not need a listener bit.
336: 
337: This is what makes **any element** (a `Text`, a `VStack`, …) able to emit
338: events — the renderer attaches native input recognition to the matching native
339: element when the listener bit is set, not only to buttons. A renderer SHOULD
340: report `POINTER_DOWN`/`POINTER_UP` for a node with the `POINTER_DOWN`/
341: `POINTER_UP` bits set by attaching a native click/press gesture to that
342: element.
343: 
344: | Command | Value | A | B | C | Flags | Description |
345: |---------|-------|---|---|---|-------|-------------|
346: | `POINTER_DOWN` | `0x01` | targetId | x (f32) | y (f32) | `POINTER_SECONDARY` | Pointer button pressed at viewport-relative point |
347: | `POINTER_MOVE` | `0x02` | targetId | x (f32) | y (f32) | `HOVER_ENTER` / `HOVER_LEAVE` | Pointer moved (bit 0 = entered/hovering, bit 1 = leaving) |
348: | `POINTER_UP` | `0x03` | targetId | x (f32) | y (f32) | `POINTER_SECONDARY` | Pointer button released at viewport-relative point |
349: | `KEY_DOWN` | `0x04` | targetId | keyCode (u16, low) | modifiers (u8, low) | `KEY_REPEAT` | Key pressed (bit 1 = auto-repeat) |
350: | `KEY_UP` | `0x05` | targetId | keyCode (u16, low) | modifiers (u8, low) | — | Key released |
351: | `VALUE_CHANGED` | `0x06` | targetId | value (f32) | 0 | — | A value-bearing control changed (e.g. slider); the renderer resolves the semantic value from its track geometry |
352: | `TEXT_CHANGED` | `0x07` | targetId | string offset | 0 | — | A text field's value changed; the new text is a length-prefixed entry in the **event arena** (shared memory, absolute `B` offset) or the batch's string section (network, *relative* `B` offset) — the same dual convention as `STYLE::SET_TEXT` |
353: | `NAVIGATE` | `0x0E` | 0 | URL string offset | 0 | `NAVIGATE_URL` | Global navigation request: with the flag, `B` is the destination URL (browser `popstate`/back/forward/deep-link, same dual string convention as `TEXT_CHANGED`); without the flag, "back one step" (native back affordance). Never node-keyed, never `EVENT_LISTENERS`-gated — see [EVENTS.md](./EVENTS.md#navigation) |
354: 
355: ### META (0x04)
356: 
357: | Command | Value | A | B | C | Description |
358: |---------|-------|---|---|---|-------------|
359: | `RESET` | `0x01` | 0 | 0 | 0 | Host must clear all rendered output |
360: | `ENVIRONMENT` | `0x02` | fieldId (u16, low) | field value | 0 | A platform environment field (host → guest) — see [Environment fields](#environment-fields) |
361: | `RESYNC` | `0x03` | 0 | 0 | 0 | The host (renderer) requests a **full snapshot** of the current tree (host → guest). The guest answers with a single full-snapshot batch (the same TREE + STYLE stream as a mount). Used for reconnect/gap recovery and no-JS refresh. |
362: 
363: #### Environment fields
364: 
365: `META::ENVIRONMENT` is an **extensible field family** (mirroring
366: `STYLE::SET_PROPERTY`): each opcode sets one platform environment field, so
367: any number of fields ride one batch and new fields are new ids — never new
368: commands. The platform (renderer / DOM client / SSR host) delivers the
369: application's launch context this way; an HTTP request supplies what it offers,
370: and the WebSocket connection **enriches** the environment after connect
371: (viewport, native deep-links, and future fields all arrive the same way).
372: 
373: | Field | Value | `B` encoding | Notes |
374: |-------|-------|--------------|-------|
375: | `VIEWPORT_WIDTH` | `0x0001` | f32 | Logical points |
376: | `VIEWPORT_HEIGHT` | `0x0002` | f32 | Logical points |
377: | `ROUTE` | `0x0003` | string offset | The initial route/deep-link path. String convention is the `TEXT_CHANGED`/`NAVIGATE` dual: absolute offset into the host → guest **event arena** over the shared ring, *relative* offset into the batch's string section over the network. |
378: 
379: **Delivery** (spec DSL.md §4.5): on SSR the host synthesizes the environment
380: from the HTTP request (`ROUTE` = request path — all the request offers); over
381: the WebSocket the DOM client sends it (viewport + `ROUTE`) as its first message
382: and re-sends it to **enrich** after connect (a window-resize re-emits the
383: viewport fields). The application applies the environment uniformly — the
384: router hydrates from the `ROUTE` field before mount, so a deep-link renders
385: correctly on the first frame.

389: ## Reactive Emission
390: 
391: The engine emits **only what changed** relative to its previous emission:
392: 
393: - **Property diff**: a changed `spacing`/`padding`/`WIDTH`/`HEIGHT`/`ALIGNMENT`/
394:   text emits a single `SET_PROPERTY` / `SET_TEXT` for that node. (Padding is a
395:   styling modifier, but it still diffs and emits like any other property.)
396: - **Structural diff**: a node added/removed/moved emits the corresponding
397:   `TREE` opcode(s).
398: - **Steady state**: an unchanged tree emits **zero** opcodes.
399: 
400: The **`frame` compound modifier** (width/height/alignment) is not a distinct
401: protocol concept: it emits `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT`/`ALIGNMENT` as ordinary
402: `STYLE:SET_PROPERTY` deltas, exactly like any other constraint property. There
403: is no `frame` opcode or dedicated wire type.
404: 
405: Signals in the application drive this: a signal marks the tree dirty; the
406: engine's next `emit` reconciles and writes only the delta. The renderer applies
407: each frame as a delta to its native elements.
408: 
409: ---
410: 
411: ## Linear Memory Layout
412: 
413: The guest engine and host share a **single linear memory**. Regions are fixed at module start:
414: 
415: ```
416: +───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────+
417: | 0x0000  Header block (80 B)  — cursors, frame counter, layout  |
418: | 0x0050  Ring buffer (16 B × slotCount)   [guest → host]        |
419: | ...      (slots densely packed, 64-byte aligned base)          |
420: | 0x10050 Event ring buffer (16 B × slotCount) [host → guest]    |
421: | ...                                                           |
422: | 0x20050 Arena (bump region, guest-owned: strings / tokens)     |
423: | ...                                                           |
424: | 0x30050 Event arena (bump region, host-owned: event strings)   |
425: | ...                                                            |
426: +───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────+
427: ```
428: 
429: > The event ring is the **host → guest** direction of the shared-memory
430: > transport: the renderer writes `EVENT`-category opcodes here and the
431: > guest/app drains them. It uses the same 16-byte slot layout as the main
432: > (guest → host) ring; both share `slotCount` (same capacity).
433: >
434: > The **event arena** is the host-owned bump region that makes strings flow
435: > **host → guest** over the shared ring: a renderer bump-allocates `TEXT_CHANGED`
436: > text (and any future string-bearing event payload) here and references it by
437: > its absolute byte offset — exactly mirroring how the guest uses the guest
438: > arena for `SET_TEXT` / STRING properties. The host resets its cursor on
439: > `META::RESET`; if the event arena is full the host applies backpressure
440: > (drops/stalls the event), mirroring ring backpressure.
441: 
442: ### Header block (80 bytes)
443: 
444: | Offset | Size | Field | Producer | Description |
445: |--------|------|-------|----------|-------------|
446: | 0x00 | 4 | `magic` | — | `0x504C504C` (`PLPL`) |
447: | 0x04 | 2 | `version` | — | Wire protocol version (1) |
448: | 0x06 | 4 | `ringOffset` | — | Byte offset of the ring region |
449: | 0x0A | 4 | `ringBytes` | — | Byte length of the ring region |
450: | 0x0E | 4 | `slotCount` | — | Number of ring slots (power of two) |
451: | 0x12 | 4 | `arenaOffset` | — | Byte offset of the arena region |
452: | 0x16 | 4 | `arenaBytes` | — | Byte length of the arena region |
453: | 0x1A | 4 | `arenaCursor` | guest | Next free byte in the arena |
454: | 0x1E | 4 | `readCursor` | host | Ring slot the host has consumed up to |
455: | 0x22 | 4 | `writeCursor` | guest | Ring slot the guest has written up to |
456: | 0x26 | 4 | `frameCount` | guest | Monotonic completed-frame counter |
457: | 0x2A | 4 | `eventRingOffset` | — | Byte offset of the host→guest event ring region |
458: | 0x2E | 4 | `eventRingBytes` | — | Byte length of the event ring region |
459: | 0x32 | 4 | `eventSlotCount` | — | Event ring slot count (power of two; = `slotCount`) |
460: | 0x36 | 4 | `eventReadCursor` | guest | Event ring slot the guest has consumed up to |
461: | 0x3A | 4 | `eventWriteCursor` | host | Event ring slot the host has written up to |
462: | 0x40 | 4 | `eventArenaOffset` | — | Byte offset of the host→guest event arena region |
463: | 0x44 | 4 | `eventArenaBytes` | — | Byte length of the event arena region |
464: | 0x48 | 4 | `eventArenaCursor` | host | Next free byte in the event arena |
465: 
466: ### Ring buffer
467: 
468: - Contiguous array of **16-byte slots**; `slotCount` is a **power of two** (wrap via mask, no modulo).
469: - **Producer** (guest) writes at `writeCursor`, then advances `writeCursor` and increments `frameCount` at frame end.
470: - **Consumer** (host) reads from `readCursor` up to `writeCursor`; after draining a frame it advances `readCursor`.
471: - **Backpressure**: the producer must not advance `writeCursor` past `readCursor` (ring full). The producer SHOULD flush a frame before the ring is full.
472: - **Frame boundary detection**: the host watches `frameCount`. When it advances, exactly one frame (all slots from the previously consumed `readCursor` to the current `writeCursor`) is complete.
473: 
474: ### Event ring (host → guest)
475: 
476: - The **host** (renderer) is the producer: it writes `EVENT`-category opcodes at `eventWriteCursor`.
477: - The **guest** (app/engine) is the consumer: it reads from `eventReadCursor` up to `eventWriteCursor`, then advances `eventReadCursor`.
478: - Events are raw inputs and are consumed as soon as they are written (no frame batching); `eventFrameCount` is not required.
479: - Backpressure mirrors the main ring: the host must not advance `eventWriteCursor` past `eventReadCursor`.
480: 
481: ### Arena
482: 
483: - A pre-allocated **bump region** for variable-length data (strings, token paths).
484: - Every arena entry is **self-describing**: `[u32 byteLength][bytes...]`.
485: - Opcodes reference entries by their **byte offset** (`arenaRef`), so an entry's length is read directly from the arena — all opcodes stay 16 bytes.
486: - The guest advances `arenaCursor` monotonically (no free-list, no fragmentation). The arena MAY be reset via `META::RESET`.
487: 
488: ### Event arena (host → guest)
489: 
490: The event arena is the **host-owned mirror** of the arena, giving the shared-memory
491: transport a host → guest string section so strings flow **both ways on all
492: transports**:
493: 
494: - The **host** (renderer) bump-allocates event string payloads here (e.g. the
495:   new text of a `TEXT_CHANGED`) and references them by their **absolute byte
496:   offset** in the event opcode — the same `SET_TEXT` shared-memory convention
497:   used in the guest arena.
498: - The **guest** resolves the text from the event arena region when draining
499:   events (`EVENT::TEXT_CHANGED`).
500: - Entries share the same self-describing `[u32 byteLength][bytes...]` layout as
501:   the guest arena.
502: - The host advances `eventArenaCursor` monotonically and resets it on
503:   `META::RESET`; a full event arena is backpressure (the host drops/stalls the
504:   event until the guest drains or a reset lands).
505: - Over the **network**, host → guest string payloads use the batch's string
506:   section with *relative* offsets instead (see [Transport](#transport)) — the
507:   same dual absolute/relative convention as `SET_TEXT`.
508: 
509: ---
510: 
511: ## Colors
512: 
513: Literal colors are **sRGB** (IEC 61966-2-1, D65 white point), packed as `0xAARRGGBB`:
514: 
515: - `AA`: alpha (0x00 transparent – 0xFF opaque)
516: - `RR`: red, `GG`: green, `BB`: blue
517: 
518: Stored little-endian in a `u32` payload. A color **property** may alternatively carry a `DESIGN_TOKEN` reference to a token path instead of a literal (see [Design Token System](#design-token-system)); semantic token resolution and theme adaptation remain **renderer-owned**.
519: 
520: ---
521: 
522: ## Design Token System
523: 
524: ### Core Principle
525: 
526: > **The application owns the theme. The renderer owns the defaults, the scheme
527: > detection, and the interaction states.**
528: 
529: - The **application** declares a theme: token overrides (base = **light**
530:   design, `dark.`-prefixed = **dark** design) and token references in style
531:   properties.
532: - The **renderer** supplies platform-appropriate defaults, derives the
533:   effective color scheme from the platform, resolves token references, and
534:   owns hover/pressed/focus/disabled styling.
535: 
536: This ensures a native look-and-feel by default and cross-platform consistency
537: when the application rolls a theme.
538: 
539: ### Tokens & color schemes
540: 
541: - Tokens are identified by **dot-separated string paths** (`color.primary`,
542:   `font.body.size`, `space.2`), case-sensitive, lowercase recommended. The
543:   `DESIGN_TOKEN` value type (`0x08`) references a token path stored in the
544:   arena; `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` overrides a token's value globally.
545: - **Base = light. `dark.`-prefixed paths are the dark variant** (`dark.color.primary`).
546:   The renderer derives the effective scheme (light/dark) from the platform and
547:   re-resolves when it changes — scheme selection is never carried by the
548:   protocol.
549: - The **standard token catalog** (colors, typography, spacing, radii,
550:   elevations, `control.*`, per-component tokens) and the **resolution
551:   algorithm** (dark layer → override → default → parent → fallback) are defined
552:   in **[TOKENS.md](./TOKENS.md)**.
553: 
554: ### References in properties
555: 
556: Any property whose value type is `COLOR` / `F32` / `STRING` / `ENUM` MAY instead
557: carry the **`DESIGN_TOKEN`** value type (`0x08`), with `C` = arenaRef to the
558: token path. The renderer resolves the reference against the token tables and the
559: current scheme. A property carries exactly one value — a literal or a token
560: reference, never both. Because overrides and the scheme are renderer state, a
561: token-typed property requires **no re-emission** when a token changes.
562: 
563: ### Renderer Responsibilities
564: 
565: The renderer MUST:
566: 
567: 1. Provide platform-appropriate **light and dark defaults** for all Tier 1 tokens.
568: 2. Accept `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` commands and store overrides.
569: 3. Derive the effective color scheme from the platform and re-resolve on change.
570: 4. Resolve token references (`DESIGN_TOKEN` value type) in properties.
571: 5. Fall back to defaults when no override exists.
572: 6. Never transmit visual styling rules in the protocol.
573: 
574: The application MAY override any token via `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` (base and `dark.*`)
575: and reference tokens via the `DESIGN_TOKEN` value type; it MUST NOT assume
576: specific default token values. Tokens a renderer cannot apply are ignored (the
577: same "allowed and ignored" rule as unapplicable modifiers).
578: 
579: ---
580: 
581: ## Frame Lifecycle
582: 
583: A frame is a batch of delta opcodes produced by one `emit` pass:
584: 
585: 1. Guest begins a frame.
586: 2. Guest emits the delta opcodes (tree structure and/or property changes) into consecutive ring slots.
587: 3. Guest allocates strings in the arena as needed.
588: 4. Guest `end_frame()`: publishes `writeCursor`, then increments `frameCount`.
589: 5. Host observes `frameCount` change, drains `[readCursor, writeCursor)`, advances `readCursor`.
590: 
591: Because the ring and arena are plain memory, the guest publishes via a single release store of `frameCount`; the host acquires on read.
592: 
593: ---
594: 
595: ## Transport
596: 
597: The opcode protocol is transport-agnostic. Two peer backends carry frames from
598: producer (guest engine) to consumer (host renderer):
599: 
600: | Backend | Scenario | Mechanism |
601: |---------|----------|-----------|
602: | Shared memory | Desktop / native (guest + host share linear memory) | The ring buffer + arena above; zero-copy |
603: | Network batch | SSR → browser (guest and host do **not** share memory) | Serialized batches of opcodes + arena delta |
604: 
605: The `Frame` type is the **transport seam**: a consumer (renderer) applies a
606: frame the same way whether it came from the shared-memory ring or a decoded
607: network batch.
608: 
609: ### Network batch format
610: 
611: ```
612: [u32 magic "PLPL"] [u16 version] [u16 flags] [u32 frameCount] [u32 opcodeCount]
613: [opcode × opcodeCount (16 B each)]
614: [u32 arenaDeltaLen] [arena delta bytes]
615: ```
616: 
617: - **magic / version**: `0x504C504C` (`PLPL`, little-endian on the wire) / `1`.
618:   A decoder MUST reject batches with a mismatched magic or version.
619: - **flags**: direction. `0x0000` = guest → host (tree/style). Bit `0x0001` =
620:   host → guest (raw-input events); host → guest batches carry their string
621:   payloads in the batch's string section.
622: - **frameCount**: the guest frame counter of the batch's first frame (opcodes
623:   from multiple frames may coalesce into one batch; they remain in order).
624: - **arena delta**: the bytes appended to the bump arena since the previous
625:   batch. The consumer keeps a **mirrored arena** and appends each delta, so
626:   absolute `arenaRef` offsets stay valid — identical to shared memory.
627: - **META::RESET**: a batch containing a reset opcode clears the consumer's
628:   mirrored arena before appending (offsets restart at 0).
629: 
630: ### Batching policy
631: 
632: The producer buffers opcodes and flushes a batch when **either** threshold is
633: reached (first trigger wins):
634: 
635: - **Time**: the interval since the first buffered opcode elapses (default **4 ms**).
636: - **Size**: the accumulated batch reaches a network-frame size (default **1400 bytes**).
637: 
638: Both thresholds are configurable; a producer MAY flush eagerly (e.g. on the
639: first frame after connection).
640: 
641: ---
642: 
643: ## Conformance
644: 
645: Golden byte vectors for this protocol are in [CONFORMANCE.md](./CONFORMANCE.md).
646: 
647: ### Companion specifications
648: 
649: The protocol's semantic surface is catalogued in four companion documents:
650: [PRIMITIVES.md](./PRIMITIVES.md) (the primitive views), [MODIFIERS.md](./MODIFIERS.md)
651: (the core modifiers, i.e. the `STYLE` properties), [EVENTS.md](./EVENTS.md)
652: (the core events, i.e. the raw inputs), and [TOKENS.md](./TOKENS.md) (the design
653: tokens / theming contract). IDs are allocated there spec-first;
654: this file remains the wire-format authority and must be updated when new IDs
655: land.
656: 
657: > **Implementation status** is tracked per implementing project (a `status.md`
658: > in each protocol crate/library), **not** in this specification. This document
659: > defines the protocol contract only.

(End of file - total 659 lines)

1: # Pathland Core Events
2: 
3: **Wire protocol version:** 1
4: **Status:** Draft
5: **Last Updated:** September 3, 2026
6: 
7: ---
8: 
9: ## Purpose
10: 
11: This document is the **catalog of core events** the Pathland protocol supports.
12: Events are the **raw inputs** a renderer reports about the user's interaction —
13: pointer motion, keys, value changes, text edits, scroll. Only the **core
14: events** are specified here; **gestures** (tap, long-press, drag, magnify,
15: rotate) are explicitly **out of scope** and are composed application-side from
16: the raw pointer events (see [Deferred: gestures](#deferred-gestures)).
17: 
18: - View catalog: [PRIMITIVES.md](./PRIMITIVES.md)
19: - Modifiers (properties): [MODIFIERS.md](./MODIFIERS.md)
20: - Wire format: [OPCODE.md](./OPCODE.md)
21: 
22: > **Implementation status** is tracked per implementing project (a `status.md`
23: > in each protocol crate/library), **not** in this specification. This document
24: > defines the protocol contract only.
25: 
26: ---
27: 
28: ## Event model
29: 
30: Events flow **host → guest**. The renderer is the producer; the app/engine is
31: the consumer. Both directions of the protocol are binary and share the same
32: 16-byte opcode format; events are `EVENT`-category (0x03) opcodes.
33: 
34: ### Who emits what
35: 
36: - The **renderer** observes native input (a GTK controller, a DOM listener) and
37:   writes raw `EVENT` opcodes. It never interprets them into high-level actions.
38: - The **app** drains the events, composes gestures/handlers, and updates its
39:   bound `State` signals (which in turn re-emit `SET_PROPERTY`/`SET_TEXT`
40:   deltas).
41: - The renderer reports an event for a node **only if that node declared it**
42:   wants it, via the `EVENT_LISTENERS` semantic property (`0x2005`, a u32
43:   bitmask, `SET_PROPERTY` with the `U32` value type). This makes **any element**
44:   (a `Text`, a `VStack`, …) able to emit events, not just controls.
45: 
46: ### Transport-aware event guards (MUST)
47: 
48: Renderers **MUST** implement event guards to prevent network noise. A user
49: interaction — tap, text change, drag, value edit — **MUST NEVER** produce an
50: outbound event opcode unless the target node explicitly declared intent in **at
51: least one** of these ways:
52: 
53: 1. it set the matching `EVENT_LISTENERS` (0x2005) bits, **or**
54: 2. it is a **value-bearing control** reporting by component type (`SLIDER`,
55:    `TOGGLE`, `PICKER`, `MENU`, `DATE_PICKER`, `COLOR_PICKER`, …), **or**
56: 3. it carries a bound callback property — `ACTION_ID` (0x2016) or `BINDING_ID`
57:    (0x2017) — that identifies where the interaction must be routed.
58: 
59: Interactions that match none of these are **dropped at the renderer**; they are
60: never serialized to the event ring or a network batch. This is the wire-level
61: guard: a `Button` tap with no `ACTION_ID`, no `BINDING_ID`, and no
62: `EVENT_LISTENERS` produces no events.
63: 
64: ### Target resolution
65: 
66: The renderer resolves `targetId` from its own rendered-output tree (its
67: `id → native element` map): the event's position is hit-tested against that
68: tree to find the deepest node with the matching listener bit. If no listener is
69: declared, the event is not reported.
70: 
71: ### Transport paths
72: 
73: | Path | Mechanism |
74: |------|-----------|
75: | Shared memory (desktop/native) | The host writes `EVENT` opcodes into the event ring (host → guest) at `eventWriteCursor`; the guest drains at `eventReadCursor`. Events are consumed as written (no frame batching). |
76: | Network batch (SSR → browser) | Host → guest batches use the `0x0001` direction flag of the `PLPL` batch format (see OPCODE.md Transport) |
77: 
78: ### Encoding
79: 
80: Every event is a 16-byte opcode:
81: 
82: ```
83: [Category=0x03][Command: u8][Flags: u16][A: u32][B: u32][C: u32]
84: ```
85: 
86: `TEXT_CHANGED` is the exception: its payload is an offset into the host → guest
87: event arena (shared memory) or the batch's string section (network), so it is
88: only fully decodable with that string source (the same convention as
89: `STYLE::SET_TEXT`).
90: 
91: ---
92: 
93: ## Core event catalog
94: 
95: ### Pointer
96: 
97: Pointer events carry a viewport-relative point in **logical points** (`B`=x,
98: `C`=y, f32).
99: 
100: | Command | Value | A | B | C | Flags | SwiftUI counterpart |
101: | --------- | ------- | --- | --- | --- | ------- | --------------------- |
102: | `POINTER_DOWN` | 0x01 | targetId | x (f32) | y (f32) | `POINTER_SECONDARY` (0x0001) | press (basis of `onTapGesture`, `Button` action) |
103: | `POINTER_MOVE` | 0x02 | targetId | x (f32) | y (f32) | `HOVER_ENTER` (0x0001) / `HOVER_LEAVE` (0x0002) | hover/enter/leave, drag basis |
104: | `POINTER_UP` | 0x03 | targetId | x (f32) | y (f32) | `POINTER_SECONDARY` (0x0001) | release (basis of `onTapGesture`) |
105: 
106: - **Flags**:
107:   - `POINTER_SECONDARY`: the secondary button (right mouse, long-press) rather
108:     than the primary.
109:   - `HOVER_ENTER` (bit 0 of `POINTER_MOVE`): the pointer just entered the
110:     node's bounds (is now hovering). `HOVER_LEAVE` (bit 1): the pointer just
111:     left. A plain move has neither bit set.
112: - **Listener bits**: `POINTER_DOWN` (bit 0), `POINTER_MOVE` (bit 1),
113:   `POINTER_UP` (bit 2).
114: - **Renderer**: attaches native press/hover recognition to the matching native
115:   element when the listener bit is set. Multiple pointer events may be reported
116:   for one physical gesture (down → several moves → up), all for the same
117:   `targetId` while the pointer stays over the node.
118: 
119: ### Keyboard
120: 
121: | Command | Value | A | B | C | Flags | SwiftUI counterpart |
122: | --------- | ------- | --- | --- | --- | ------- | --------------------- |
123: | `KEY_DOWN` | 0x04 | targetId | keyCode (u16, low) | modifiers (u8, low) | `KEY_REPEAT` (0x0002) | `onKeyPress(.down)` |
124: | `KEY_UP` | 0x05 | targetId | keyCode (u16, low) | modifiers (u8, low) | — | `onKeyPress(.up)` |
125: 
126: - **`keyCode`**: a **canonical, platform-independent logical key code** (a
127:   renderer maps native scancodes/key-codes onto this canonical set). The
128:   canonical set (letters/digits/arrows/Enter/Tab/…) is renderer-shared and
129:   documented in the conformance vectors.
130: - **`modifiers`**: u8 bitmask — `Shift`=0x01, `Control`=0x02, `Alt`=0x04,
131:   `Meta/Super`=0x08.
132: - **`KEY_REPEAT`**: bit 1 of flags; set when the key is an OS auto-repeat.
133: - **Listener bits**: `KEY_DOWN` (bit 3), `KEY_UP` (bit 4).
134: - **Focus**: keyboard events are reported to the focused node (the node that
135:   most recently gained focus), or to the node that declared the listener and
136:   has keyboard focus. See `FOCUS_CHANGED` below.
137: 
138: ### Value
139: 
140: Value events carry a control's semantic value, resolved by the renderer from
141: its own native control geometry.
142: 
143: | Command | Value | A | B | C | Flags | SwiftUI counterpart |
144: | --------- | ------- | --- | --- | --- | ------- | --------------------- |
145: | `VALUE_CHANGED` | 0x06 | targetId | value (f32) | 0 | — | `Slider`/`Stepper`/`Gauge`/`Toggle`/`Picker`/`Menu` binding changes |
146: 
147: - **Semantics per control** (see [PRIMITIVES.md](./PRIMITIVES.md) controls):
148:   - `SLIDER`/`STEPPER`/`GAUGE` — the numeric value in the control's range.
149:   - `TOGGLE` — 0/1 (checked state; the same value the app writes to
150:     `SELECTED`).
151:   - `PICKER`/`MENU` — the selected option/action-item index.
152:   - `COLOR_PICKER` — the packed `0xAARRGGBB` color reinterpreted as an f32 bit
153:     pattern.
154:   - `DATE_PICKER` uses the dedicated `DATE_CHANGED` event below (its value is
155:     two fields and does not fit `VALUE_CHANGED`).
156: - The app writes the received value into its bound `State`; the engine's
157:   signal flush re-emits the `SET_PROPERTY` delta back to the renderer (the
158:   renderer reflects its own native control).
159: - **No listener bit**: value-bearing controls are reported by the renderer by
160:   virtue of their component type, but still gated by the transport-aware event
161:   guards (a control without `BINDING_ID` reports nothing). The renderer owns
162:   the gesture (e.g. slider drag) that produces them.
163: 
164: ### Date
165: 
166: | Command | Value | A | B | C | Flags | SwiftUI counterpart |
167: | --------- | ------- | --- | --- | --- | ------- | --------------------- |
168: | `DATE_CHANGED` | 0x0D | targetId | days since epoch (I32) | millis of day (U32) | — | `DatePicker` value binding |
169: 
170: - The date is encoded as two 32-bit fields — `B` = **days since epoch**
171:   (signed I32; pre-1970 is negative) and `C` = **millis of day** (U32,
172:   0..86,400,000) — matching the `STYLE::SET_DATE` command (OPCODE.md). No
173:   string/arena indirection: the event is fully inline. It works over the
174:   shared-memory ring today and will use the same inline encoding for host →
175:   guest network batches once that direction lands (see OPCODE.md Transport).
176: - **No listener bit**: like `VALUE_CHANGED`, reported by virtue of the
177:   component type.
178: 
179: ### Text
180: 
181: | Command | Value | A | B | C | Flags | SwiftUI counterpart |
182: | --------- | ------- | --- | --- | --- | ------- | --------------------- |
183: | `TEXT_CHANGED` | 0x07 | targetId | string offset | 0 | — | `TextField` value binding |
184: | `FOCUS_CHANGED` | 0x08 | targetId | focused (0/1) | 0 | — | `@FocusState` |
185: | `EDITING_CHANGED` | 0x09 | targetId | editing (0/1) | 0 | — | `TextField`/`Slider` `onEditingChanged` |
186: | `SUBMIT` | 0x0A | targetId | 0 | 0 | — | `TextField` `onSubmit` / `onCommit` |
187: 
188: - **`TEXT_CHANGED`**: the new text is a length-prefixed entry
189:   (`[u32 byteLength][bytes…]`). Over the **shared-memory ring** the renderer
190:   bump-allocates it into the host-owned **event arena** and `B` is its absolute
191:   offset (see OPCODE.md); over the **network** it lives in the batch's string
192:   section referenced by a *relative* `B` offset — exactly the `STYLE::SET_TEXT`
193:   dual convention. A bare opcode cannot resolve the text; batch-aware decoders
194:   (`pathland-core-transport`, Java `FrameCodec`, TS `decoder.ts`) resolve it.
195:   The event is reported on **every** edit, including intermediate edits, not
196:   only on commit.
197: - **`FOCUS_CHANGED`**: `B` = 1 gained focus, 0 lost focus. The renderer reports
198:   it for nodes that declared the `FOCUS` listener bit (bit 5). Focus is what
199:   routes subsequent `KEY_*` events.
200: - **`EDITING_CHANGED`**: `B` = 1 editing session began, 0 ended. Reported for
201:   nodes that declared the `EDITING` listener bit (bit 6).
202: - **`SUBMIT`**: the user committed the field (Enter). Reported for nodes that
203:   declared the `SUBMIT` listener bit (bit 7). `B` MAY carry the current text as
204:   a string-section offset (reserved for future use; 0 today).
205: 
206: ### Scroll
207: 
208: | Command | Value | A | B | C | Flags | SwiftUI counterpart |
209: | --------- | ------- | --- | --- | --- | ------- | --------------------- |
210: | `SCROLL` | 0x0B | targetId | offsetX (f32) | offsetY (f32) | — | `ScrollView` offset, `onScrollPhaseChange` |
211: | `WHEEL` | 0x0C | targetId | deltaX (f32) | deltaY (f32) | — | `onScrollWheelEvent` / trackpad |
212: 
213: - **`SCROLL`**: the content offset of a `SCROLLVIEW` (logical points), reported
214:   for nodes that declared the `SCROLL` listener bit (bit 8). The renderer
215:   reports the absolute offset after each scroll delta.
216: - **`WHEEL`**: raw wheel/trackpad deltas (logical points), reported for nodes
217:   that declared the `WHEEL` listener bit (bit 9). Renderers map native scroll
218:   deltas (GTK `GtkEventControllerScroll`, DOM `wheel`) onto x/y deltas.
219: 
220: ### Navigation
221: 
222: | Command | Value | A | B | C | Flags | SwiftUI counterpart |
223: | --------- | ------- | --- | --- | --- | ------- | --------------------- |
224: | `NAVIGATE` | 0x0E | 0 | URL string offset | 0 | `NAVIGATE_URL` (0x0001) | browser back/forward (`popstate`), a deep link, or a native back affordance |
225: 
226: - **`NAVIGATE` is a global event — never node-gated.** It carries **no
227:   `targetId`** (`A` = 0) and is **not** subject to `EVENT_LISTENERS` or the
228:   transport-aware event guards: the renderer/host emits it only when the
229:   application has registered a navigation handler (a `Router`), and it is
230:   delivered directly to that handler. See [DSL.md §4.5](./DSL.md#45-navigation).
231: - **With a URL** (`NAVIGATE_URL` flag set): `B` is a string-section / event-arena
232:   offset to the destination URL the platform navigated to — a browser
233:   `popstate` (back/forward), a deep link, or a renderer-originated URL. The
234:   host calls `router.handlePlatformNavigation(url)`, which matches and re-emits.
235: - **Without a URL** (flag clear): the platform back affordance (Android
236:   predictive-back, iOS swipe-back, a desktop back button) — the host calls
237:   `router.pop()`. The renderer never decides navigation; it only requests it.
238: - The string encoding follows the exact `TEXT_CHANGED` dual convention: over
239:   the **shared-memory ring** the renderer bump-allocates the URL into the
240:   host-owned event arena and `B` is its absolute offset; over the **network**
241:   it lives in the batch's string section referenced by a *relative* `B` offset.
242:   The `NAVIGATE_URL` flag distinguishes "URL at `B`" from "back one step" even
243:   when `B` would otherwise be a valid offset.
244: 
245: ---
246: 
247: ## Event listeners (`EVENT_LISTENERS`)
248: 
249: `EVENT_LISTENERS` (0x2005) is a u32 bitmask set via `SET_PROPERTY` (U32). Each
250: bit requests one raw-input event kind for the node:
251: 
252: | Bit | Mask | Event |
253: | ----- | ------ | ------- |
254: | 0 | `0x00000001` | `POINTER_DOWN` |
255: | 1 | `0x00000002` | `POINTER_MOVE` (incl. hover enter/leave) |
256: | 2 | `0x00000004` | `POINTER_UP` |
257: | 3 | `0x00000008` | `KEY_DOWN` |
258: | 4 | `0x00000010` | `KEY_UP` |
259: | 5 | `0x00000020` | `FOCUS_CHANGED` |
260: | 6 | `0x00000040` | `EDITING_CHANGED` |
261: | 7 | `0x00000080` | `SUBMIT` |
262: | 8 | `0x00000100` | `SCROLL` |
263: | 9 | `0x00000200` | `WHEEL` |
264: | 10–31 | — | reserved |
265: 
266: Convenience aliases (DSL-side): `POINTER = bits 0|1|2`.
267: 
268: DSL surfaces:
269: 
270: - Rust: `pathland_view::pointer_events(mask)` modifier + `listener::*` bits;
271:   `on_tap_gesture` sets `POINTER_DOWN | POINTER_UP`.
272: - Java: `TapGestureView` / `EVENT_LISTENERS` via the emitter; host forwards raw
273:   `EVENT` batches into bound `State` signals.
274: 
275: ---
276: 
277: ## Deferred: gestures
278: 
279: SwiftUI gestures — `onTapGesture`, `onLongPressGesture`, `DragGesture`,
280: `MagnifyGesture`, `RotateGesture` — are **not protocol events**. Per the
281: protocol's raw-inputs-only rule, they are **composed application-side** from
282: the raw `POINTER_*` / `KEY_*` events above:
283: 
284: - **Tap** = `POINTER_DOWN` then `POINTER_UP` on the same `targetId` within the
285:   platform's tap window.
286: - **Long-press** = `POINTER_DOWN` held past a threshold.
287: - **Drag** = `POINTER_DOWN` + `POINTER_MOVE` sequence.
288: - **Magnify / rotate** = multi-pointer deltas; the underlying raw events are
289:   `POINTER_*` (multi-touch reported per pointer).
290: 
291: A future "gesture recognition" layer MAY define app-side recognizers, but the
292: wire protocol will never carry interpreted gestures — only raw inputs.
293: 
294: ---
295: 
296: ## Reserved event command IDs
297: 
298: | Range | Use |
299: |-------|-----|
300: | `0x01`–`0x0E` | Core events (allocated, this file) |
301: | `0x0F`–`0x3F` | Future core events (unallocated) |
302: | `0x40`–`0xFF` | Custom/application events |
303: 
304: A renderer/decoder MUST skip unknown event commands and continue.
305: 
306: ---
307: 
308: ## Conformance
309: 
310: Event encode/decode round-trips and golden byte vectors (incl. raw-input
311: `EVENT` and network-batch bytes) live in [CONFORMANCE.md](./CONFORMANCE.md).
312: New events added here MUST add vectors before implementation.

(End of file - total 312 lines)
</content>

273: ## 6. Navigation
274: 
275: Two properties support routing and URL sync. They are emitted by the
276: application's `NavigationContainer` ([DSL.md §4.5](./DSL.md#45-navigation)) and
277: are never chainable modifiers.
278: 
279: | Property | ID | Type | Emission |
280: |----------|----|------|----------|
281: | `ROUTE` | 0x2019 | STRING (arenaRef) | one — the current absolute path |
282: | `NAV_DEPTH` | 0x201A | U32 | one — current back-stack depth |
283: | `NAV_CHROME` | 0x201B | ENUM | one — chrome mode (at mount; never varies per destination) |
284: | `TRANSITION` | 0x1031 | ENUM | one — swap transition hint (see [§3](#3-appearance--effects)) |
285: 
286: - **`ROUTE`** carries the current absolute path (`/users/42`). The DOM renderer
287:   reacts to a `ROUTE` change with `history.pushState`; the initial SSR document
288:   already carries the correct URL (no push). The application owns navigation
289:   state; the browser mirrors it. The platform back affordance arrives as the
290:   `NAVIGATE` event (0x0E) — [EVENTS.md](./EVENTS.md#navigation).
291: - **`NAV_DEPTH`** is the number of destinations in the app's back-stack
292:   including the current one (an initial `navigate` is 1; each `push`
293:   increments; `pop`/`back` decrements; `replace` leaves it unchanged). It lets
294:   a **native navigation adapter** reconcile its page stack by depth —
295:   `push` when the route is new and deeper, **replace the top page** when the
296:   depth is unchanged (a guard redirect), **pop down** on a depth decrease
297:   (back or a deep-link stack reset), instead of relying on route tags alone
298:   ([DSL.md §4.5](./DSL.md#45-navigation)). The web renderer ignores it
299:   (browser history is the depth).
300: - **`NAV_CHROME`** is the container's chrome mode: `PlatformDefault`=0 (the
301:   renderer supplies the navigation chrome — the platform's native navigation
302:   container where one exists, a renderer-drawn back affordance where it does
303:   not, e.g. DOM), `Custom`=1 (the developer owns all navigation UI — custom
304:   back buttons/bars in the destinations — and the renderer adds none). Emitted
305:   once at mount. Renderers MUST treat a missing `NAV_CHROME` as
306:   `PlatformDefault`. A developer who authors no navigation at all (no
307:   `NavigationContainer`) gets no navigation — the renderer adds nothing.
308: 
309: ---
310: 
311: ## Property ID Catalog
312: 
313: ### Allocated property IDs
314: 
315: | Range | Group |
316: | ------- | ------- |
317: | `0x0001`–`0x0005` | Stack constraint (SPACING, ALIGNMENT, …, CONTENT_MARGINS) |
318: | `0x0006` | `SHAPE_KIND` (ENUM; view-specific, see PRIMITIVES.md) |
319: | `0x000A`–`0x000D` | Text (TEXT, LINE_LIMIT, TEXT_ALIGNMENT, TRUNCATION_MODE) |
320: | `0x000E`–`0x001D` | Layout properties (allocated: OFFSET, POSITION, frame bounds, FIXED_SIZE, LAYOUT_PRIORITY, ASPECT_RATIO/CONTENT_MODE, MINIMUM_SCALE_FACTOR) |
321: | `0x001E`–`0x00FF` | Future layout/format properties (unallocated) |
322: | `0x1001`–`0x1016` | Styling (BACKGROUND_COLOR, BORDER_*, FONT_SIZE/WEIGHT/FAMILY, COLOR, WIDTH, HEIGHT, OPACITY, VISIBLE, Z_INDEX, CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS, PADDING_*, BORDER_EDGES) |
323: | `0x1002` | `IMAGE_SOURCE` (STRING; view-specific, see PRIMITIVES.md) |
324: | `0x1017`–`0x102F` | Text-format properties (allocated: FONT_STYLE/DESIGN/WIDTH, KERNING, TRACKING, BASELINE_OFFSET, LINE_SPACING, TEXT_CASE, UNDERLINE, STRIKETHROUGH), effect properties (SHADOW_*, BLUR, SATURATION, CONTRAST, BRIGHTNESS, GRAYSCALE, HUE_ROTATION, COLOR_MULTIPLY, COLOR_INVERT), ROTATION_DEGREES, SCALE, ALLOWS_HIT_TESTING |
325: | `0x1030` | `TINT` (COLOR) | — |
326: | `0x1031` | `TRANSITION` (ENUM; navigation swap hint) | — |
327: | `0x1032`–`0x10FF` | Future styling properties (unallocated) |
328: | `0x2001`–`0x200B` | Semantic (ROLE, STATE, ENABLED, SELECTED, EVENT_LISTENERS, VALUE, MIN_VALUE, MAX_VALUE, LABEL, PROMPT) |
329: | `0x2009`, `0x200C`–`0x2014` | Control properties (allocated: STEP_VALUE, CONTROL_SIZE, IS_SECURE, PROGRESS, IS_INDETERMINATE, SELECTION, COLOR_VALUE, DATE_PICKER_MODE, PICKER_STYLE) — defined in PRIMITIVES.md controls. Note: a `DATE_PICKER`'s date is set via the `STYLE::SET_DATE` command (0x04), not a property; **`0x2011` is unallocated/reserved** (its former `DATE_VALUE` draft was dropped) |
330: | `0x2016`–`0x2018` | Binding/action properties (allocated: `ACTION_ID`, `BINDING_ID`, `TOGGLE_STYLE`) — defined in PRIMITIVES.md semantic controls |
331: | `0x2019` | `ROUTE` (STRING; navigation current path) — see §6 |
332: | `0x201A` | `NAV_DEPTH` (U32; navigation back-stack depth) — see §6 |
333: | `0x201B` | `NAV_CHROME` (ENUM; navigation chrome mode) — see §6 |
334: | `0x2015`, `0x201C`–`0x20FF` | Future semantic properties (unallocated) |
335: 
336: ### Reserved ranges
337: 
338: | Range | Use |
339: |-------|-----|
340: | `0x0003`, `0x0004` | Reserved (formerly JUSTIFICATION, PADDING) — MUST NOT be reused |
341: | `0x0007`–`0x0009`, `0x000E`+ high | Draft/future layout |
342: | `0x1002` | `IMAGE_SOURCE` (allocated) |
343: 
344: A renderer MUST ignore unknown property ids and continue decoding.
345: 
346: ### Default value type resolution
347: 
348: The canonical value type per property (the protocol's authoritative mapping):
349:

351:   `SHADOW_COLOR`, `COLOR_VALUE`, `TINT` → `COLOR`
