1: # pathland-render-html (Rust) — implementation status
2: 
3: **Last updated:** September 3, 2026
4: 
5: The **server-side / remote-projection HTML renderer**: a **stateless, streaming**
6: pure function of the opcode stream producing declarative HTML. Each render call
7: decodes a self-contained snapshot batch into a **transient** map, walks it once,
8: and emits HTML text out — no retained tree, zero cross-call state (Renderer
9: Statelessness). Protocol contract: `spec/`.
10: 
11: ## Implemented
12: 
13: - **Stateless streaming API**: `HtmlRenderer::render_document(opcodes, strings, root)`
14:   / `render_fragment(...)` build a transient decode map per call and stream HTML;
15:   the retained `apply`/`apply_frame`/`render` model is removed.
16: - **All spec components render**: `TEXT`, `IMAGE`, `COLOR` (layout-greedy:
17:   `flex:1;align-self:stretch`), `SHAPE` (CSS/SVG by `SHAPE_KIND`), `DIVIDER`, `SPACER`, `PROGRESS_VIEW`/`GAUGE`, `VSTACK`/
18:   `HSTACK`/`LAZY_VSTACK`/`LAZY_HSTACK` (flex), `ZSTACK` (overlay), `GRID`/
19:   `LAZY_VGRID`/`LAZY_HGRID` (CSS grid), `SCROLLVIEW`, `BUTTON`, `TEXT_FIELD`
20:   (incl. `IS_SECURE` → `type="password"`), `TEXT_EDITOR`, `TOGGLE`
21:   (`TOGGLE_STYLE`), `SLIDER`, `STEPPER`, `DATE_PICKER` (`SET_DATE` →
22:   `days_to_date`), `PICKER` (option children + `SELECTION`), `MENU`,
23:   `COLOR_PICKER`, `COMMENT`.
24: - **Composite override mode**: `BUTTON`/`TOGGLE`/`SLIDER` with children render
25:   the custom body wrapped in the native element.
26: - **Properties**: `ALIGNMENT` (cross-axis flex), `CONTENT_MARGINS`,
27:   `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` (`FILL`/`HUG`), `PADDING` + per-edge, `COLOR`,
28:   `BACKGROUND_COLOR`, `FONT_SIZE`/`WEIGHT`/`FAMILY`, `OPACITY`, `VISIBLE`,
29:   `Z_INDEX`, `LINE_LIMIT`, `TEXT_ALIGNMENT`, `TRUNCATION_MODE`, `BORDER_*`,
30:   `SELECTED`, `TOGGLE_STYLE`, `ENABLED`, `ROLE`/`STATE` (ARIA), plus
31:   `TEXT_CASE`, `FONT_STYLE`, `FONT_DESIGN`, `UNDERLINE`/`STRIKETHROUGH`,
32:   `CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS`, `ALLOWS_HIT_TESTING`, `COLOR_INVERT`.
33: - **Event surfacing**: `data-event-listeners` / `data-action-id` /
34:   `data-binding-id` attributes.
35: - **Navigation slot attrs** (spec DSL.md §4.5 / MODIFIERS.md): a slot node's
36:   `ROUTE` (STRING) renders as `data-pathland-route="<path>"`, its
37:   `TRANSITION` hint renders as `data-pathland-transition="<platform|fade|slide|scale>"`,
38:   its `NAV_CHROME` (F32 enum) renders `data-pathland-nav-chrome="custom"`
39:   when `Custom` (the renderer adds no default chrome), and `NAV_DEPTH` (U32)
40:   renders `data-pathland-depth="N"` when deeper than its root so the DOM client
41:   can hydrate its default back button from the SSR HTML — the DOM renderer
42:   mirrors the route into the URL, may animate a swap, and draws the renderer's
43:   own back button (the web has no native navigation container).
44: - `STYLE::SET_DATE` handled (days + millis-of-day → date/time).
45: - **Design tokens (spec/TOKENS.md)**:
46:   - `STYLE::SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` overrides are collected per snapshot batch and
47:     emitted into the document head as CSS: base (light) tokens as `:root`
48:     rules, `dark.*` overrides inside `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` —
49:     the browser resolves the scheme natively, so SSR needs no client scheme.
50:   - `DESIGN_TOKEN`-typed `SET_PROPERTY` values resolve at render time to
51:     `var(--pl-…)`, with the generative `space.<N>` family resolving to
52:     `calc(var(--pl-space-base) * N)` (`Node::token_ref`).
53:   - **`STRING`-valued token overrides** (e.g. `font.body.family`): a
54:     `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` with `valueType = STRING` resolves the value string from
55:     the batch's string section and emits it single-quoted (escaped) as a
56:     `:root` rule (or inside the dark media query).
57:   - The override rules render inside their own **`<style data-pathland-tokens>`**
58:     element in the document head, **after** the built-in block (so their
59:     `:root` variables win the cascade and the browser applies them) — matching
60:     the JS DOM client's `style[data-pathland-tokens]` element. No overrides →
61:     no extra element.
62:   - The built-in `:root` tokens use the **canonical spec paths** (`--pl-color-primary`,
63:     `--pl-color-background`, `--pl-color-text-primary`, `--pl-color-text-secondary`,
64:     `--pl-color-surface`, `--pl-color-border`) so app overrides retheme the
65:     renderer.
66:   - **Full Tier-1 default coverage**: `--pl-space-base` (light + dark, so the
67:     generative `space.<N>` family always resolves), canonical typography
68:     (`--pl-font-body-size/weight/family`), the radius scale + `--pl-border-width-thin`,
69:     and the **shared control core mapped onto the canonical catalog** —
70:     `--pl-control-*`, `--pl-button-*`, `--pl-input-*` (light + dark), with the
71:     focus ring mapped to `control.accent` and shadows mapped onto the composite
72:     `elevation.low.*` / `elevation.high.*` tokens. `.pathland-*` rules reference
73:     the canonical variables, so `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` overrides retheme components.
74: 
75: ## Design decision (decision A, September 2026): inline-all + built-in design system
76: 
77: Tailwind is **removed**. The renderer emits **everything inline** as CSS in a
78: single `style` attribute — no external compiler, no class system, no safelist:
79: 
80: - **All opcode properties render inline** (`style_css()` + `border_style()`),
81:   including the previously class-based enum surface (alignment, text alignment,
82:   text case, visible, font style/design, underline/strikethrough, clips-to-bounds,
83:   hit-testing, invert, truncation). **1 dp = 1 CSS px**.
84: - **`css::STYLE`** is a built-in `<style>` block injected by `render_document`,
85:   containing:
86:   - a **preflight reset** (vendored from Tailwind CSS, MIT — see
87:     `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES`),
88:   - `:root` **design tokens** as CSS custom properties (`--pl-color-primary`,
89:     `--pl-color-background` (document background), `--pl-color-surface`,
90:     `--pl-color-text-primary`/`--pl-color-text-secondary`, `--pl-color-border`,
91:     `--pl-radius-*`, `--pl-font-sans`, `--pl-input-*` (field bg/text/outline/
92:     placeholder/focus), button tokens), named to match the canonical protocol
93:     design-token paths so `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` can retheme the renderer,
94:   - `.pathland-button` (the prettified-button POC, with `prefers-color-scheme`
95:     dark mode) and `.pathland-*` component defaults (toggle switch, slider, text
96:     field/editor, stepper, spinner, gauge, menu) — the interactive/hover/focus/
97:     disabled states that can't be expressed inline. Text fields use a
98:     Tailwind-style **inset outline** (`outline: 1px solid`, `outline-offset: -1px`,
99:     focus → `2px`/`-2px` + indigo) instead of a border, with dark-mode tokens;
100:     `html` sets `color-scheme: light dark` + the `--pl-color-bg` background so
101:     native form controls and the page follow the theme.
102: - **`pathland_html_*` cdylib** (`pathland_html_render` / `_render_fragment` /
103:   `_free`) for cross-language hosts (Java JNA shim). The `_tailwind_compile`
104:   entry point, `tw.rs`, `tailwind.rs`, `build.rs`, `scripts/fetch-tailwind.mjs`,
105:   `vendor/`, and the `tailwind-embed` feature are **deleted**.
106: 
107: ## Not implemented / gaps
108: 
109: - **`DESIGN_TOKEN` property references** cover the directly-mappable subset
110:   (colors, font size/weight, spacing/padding, corner radius, opacity,
111:   width/height, border width/color, shadow color). Compound accumulators that
112:   need concrete numbers (shadow radius/x/y) remain literal-only.
113: - `SHAPE` `Path` renders as an SVG placeholder (no path data wire property).
114: - GAUGE/SHAPE visuals are CSS approximations, not pixel-exact.
115: - **Inter is loaded from the rsms.me CDN** (Cloudflare, `font-display: swap`,
116:   with the InterVariable progressive enhancement for variable-font browsers) —
117:   the renderer emits the preconnect + stylesheet links in the document head. It
118:   is **not bundled**: self-hosting a subsetted, OFL-licensed woff2 (embedded in
119:   the renderer / jar) is a planned follow-up for offline and enterprise
120:   deployments (see `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES`).

3: **Last updated:** September 14, 2026
4: 
5: Runs the shared framework-agnostic demo views (`com.pathland.demo`, e.g.

13: - The in-process GTK renderer pumps the same ring in place
14:   (`pathland_gtk_run_ring`, via `PathlandCore.ringMut`); no
15:   `pathland-view-native` host is involved.
16: - Native inputs round-trip as `EVENT` opcodes that this host drains
17:   (`pathland_core_drain_events`) and dispatches into the app's bindings via the
18:   shared `InputDispatcher` (taps, text/value/date inputs, router back).
19: - State/theme/platform seeding mirrors the server session: `PersistentState`
20:   over an `InMemoryStateStore`, `DemoTheme.adaptive()` as the emitter theme, and
21:   `Platform.ACTIVE_PATH` injected as a host signal (`/home`) — `SplitNavDemo`
22:   reads it and builds its bound router.
23:

26: - `GtkRendererNative` — JNA binding to `libpathland_gtk`
27:   (`pathland_gtk_run_ring(ring, on_event, width, height)`); library resolved

29: - `RingEventReader` — decodes raw ring `EVENT` opcodes into
30:   `com.pathland.view.transport.Event`, resolving `TEXT_CHANGED`/`NAVIGATE`

33:   bounds behaviour.

# Pathland Renderer Feasibility Assessment — Qt Renderer

## (a) Exact public / C-ABI surface a Qt renderer would need to match

### Two transport models exist; a Qt renderer can pick either

**Model 1 — "Borrowed ring" (recommended, what the Java host uses):** The renderer receives a raw pointer to a `pathland_core_transport::RingTransport` (`libpathland_core` ring) already owned by the host, and pumps it in place. Entry point:

- `pathland_gtk_run_ring(ring: *mut c_void, on_event: Option<extern "C" fn()>, width: u32, height: u32)` — `lib/rust/crates/pathland-render-gtk/src/capi.rs:118-145`. Blocks until the main loop exits. `on_event` is a **no-payload wake callback** (the host drains the event ring itself); `width`/`height` size the default window.

**Model 2 — "NativeHost" (flat world):** The renderer borrows a `pathland-view-native` `NativeHost` (which owns the retained tree, diff engine, and ring) and calls the flat `pathland_native_*` surface from within the GTK pump. Entry point:

- `pathland_gtk_run(host: *mut c_void, on_event: Option<extern "C" fn()>)` — `capi.rs:75-103`.

### The `Pump` trait — the renderer's core transport seam

`lib/rust/crates/pathland-render-gtk/src/lib.rs:52-66`:

```rust
pub trait Pump {
    fn next_frame(&mut self) -> Result<Option<OpcodeBatch<'_>>, TransportError>; // guest → host frames
    fn send_input(&mut self, event: &Event) -> Result<(), TransportError>;        // host → guest EVENT opcodes
}
```

- Implemented for `RingTransport` (`lib.rs:59-66`), for the borrowed `NativeHost` (`capi.rs:34-45`, `NativeHostHandle`), and for the borrowed core ring (`capi.rs:53-63`, `CoreRingHandle`).
- `OpcodeBatch`/`FrameSource`/`DriverTransport` are in `lib/rust/crates/pathland-core-transport/src/traits.rs:21-91`. `RingTransport` impls at `pathland-core-transport/src/ring.rs:65-97` (`FrameSource::next_frame` builds a `Host` view and returns an `OpcodeBatch`; `DriverTransport::send_input` writes an EVENT opcode into the host→guest event ring). The `drain_events()` consumer helper is at `ring.rs:90-97`.

### The C ABI a native host links against

**`libpathland_core`** (`pathland-core-capi`, `cdylib`, lib name `pathland_core`) — the minimal SPSC ring + opcode engine C ABI, `lib/rust/crates/pathland-core-capi/src/lib.rs`:

- Lifetime: `pathland_core_create()` (:58), `pathland_core_destroy()` (:67)
- Ring (guest→host): `pathland_ring_buffer_push(handle, *u8 /*16B*/)` (:81), `pathland_core_arena_alloc(handle, bytes, len)` (:93), `pathland_core_begin_frame` (:109), `pathland_core_end_frame` (:116), `pathland_core_frame_count` (:123), `pathland_core_ring_ptr` (:131), `pathland_core_ring_len` (:137), **`pathland_core_ring_mut`** (:147 — the borrow a renderer pumps)
- Events (host→guest): `pathland_core_drain_events(handle, out, max)` (:162), `pathland_core_send_event(handle, *u8 /*16B*/)` (:184)

**`libpathland_native`** (`pathland-view-native`, `cdylib`+`rlib`, lib name `pathland_native`) — the flat retained-tree world + signals, `lib/rust/crates/pathland-view-native/src/capi.rs`:

- Builder: `pathland_native_create`/`destroy` (:35/:42), `pathland_native_create_node(host, id, component)` (:59), `insert_child` (:72), `remove_child` (:83), `set_text` (:90), `set_property` (:106), `set_property_f32` (:118), `pathland_native_emit` (:135)
- Zero-copy ring: `pathland_native_ring_ptr` (:152), `ring_len` (:159), `layout_bytes` (:166), `root_id` (:173)
- Events: `pathland_native_drain_events` (:191 — writes raw 16-byte EVENT opcodes into caller buffer)
- Signals: `signal_create_f32/u32/bool/enum/string` (:219-252), `signal_set_*` (:257-307), `node_bind_text` (:312), `node_bind_property` (:322)
- Component id mapping + property value-type mapping: `component_from_id`/`property_value_type` in `lib.rs:272-360`

**GTK renderer's own cdylib** (`libpathland_gtk`, `cdylib`+`rlib`): the two `pathland_gtk_*` entry points above.

### How Java binds it (JNA)

- `PathlandCore.java` (`lib/java/pathland-view/src/main/java/com/pathland/view/ffm/PathlandCore.java:45-58`) declares the `NativePathlandCore` interface matching the `pathland_core_*` functions; lazily loads `libpathland_core` via `Native.load` (:82). It keeps a reused 16-byte `Memory` opcode buffer (:72) to avoid per-op allocations.
- `RingOpcodeSink.java` (`.../ffm/RingOpcodeSink.java`) is the Java `OpcodeSink` that writes TREE/STYLE opcodes into the ring via JNA — `createNode`, `insertChild`, `setText` (arena-allocates the string, :75), `setProperty` (encodes `B = (valueType << 16) | propertyId`, :81), `setDesignToken` (:100).
- `GtkRendererNative.java` (`lib/java/pathland-gtk-demo/src/main/java/com/pathland/demo/gtk/GtkRendererNative.java:31-33`) declares `void pathland_gtk_run_ring(Pointer ring, EventCallback onEvent, int width, int height)` and loads `libpathland_gtk` (library resolution via `-Dpathland.gtk.lib` or `java.library.path`, :72-89).
- `GtkHost.java` (`.../gtk/GtkHost.java:51-85`) is the full flow: `RingOpcodeSink` → `core.ringMut(handle)` → `pathland_gtk_run_ring(ring, onEvent, 1100, 720)`. The wake callback drains `core.drainEvents(handle, buf, 64)` and dispatches via `InputDispatcher`. macOS requires `-XstartOnFirstThread` (GTK owns the main thread).
- `RingEventReader.java` (`.../gtk/RingEventReader.java`) decodes raw EVENT opcodes on the Java side, resolving `TEXT_CHANGED`/`NAVIGATE` strings from the shared event arena at header offset `0x40` (:24, :83-97).

### A Qt renderer would need to provide

1. A `Pump` impl (or equivalent) — `next_frame` + `send_input` — either over a borrowed `RingTransport` (Qt model 1) or a `NativeHost` (Qt model 2).
2. A `pathland_qt_run` / `pathland_qt_run_ring` `extern "C" fn` with the identical signature and wake-callback contract (host drains events; renderer never drains).
3. `WidgetKind`-style component→widget mapping (below), TREE/STYLE delta application, event emission gated by `EVENT_LISTENERS`/`BINDING_ID`/`ACTION_ID`, token resolution + scheme detection, and the empty-argv pattern (see (d)).

## (b) Full opcode command set a renderer must handle

From `lib/rust/crates/pathland-core/src/constants.rs` and `spec/OPCODE.md`. Every opcode is 16 bytes: `[Category u8][Command u8][Flags u16][A u32][B u32][C u32]`, little-endian.

### Categories (`constants.rs:8-19`)
| Category | Value | Direction |
|---|---|---|
| `TREE` | 0x01 | guest → host |
| `STYLE` | 0x02 | guest → host |
| `EVENT` | 0x03 | host → guest |
| `META` | 0x04 | both |

### TREE commands (`constants.rs:22-33`)
| Command | Value | Payload |
|---|---|---|
| `CREATE_NODE` | 0x01 | `A=nodeId, B=componentType (u16 low)` |
| `DELETE_NODE` | 0x02 | `A=nodeId` |
| `INSERT_CHILD` | 0x03 | `A=parent, B=child, C=index` (append = `u32::MAX`) |
| `REMOVE_CHILD` | 0x04 | `A=parent, B=child` |
| `MOVE_CHILD` | 0x05 | `A=parent, B=child, C=newIndex` |

The GTK renderer applies these in `RenderTree::apply_frame` (`host.rs:173-270`); the HTML renderer in `apply_tree` (`pathland-render-html/src/lib.rs:691-723`).

### STYLE commands (`constants.rs:36-47`)
| Command | Value | Payload |
|---|---|---|
| `SET_PROPERTY` | 0x01 | `A=nodeId, B=(valueType<<16)\|propertyId, C=value` (STRING/DESIGN_TOKEN: C is an arena/string-section offset) |
| `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` | 0x02 | `A=arenaRef(path), B=valueType, C=value` |
| `SET_TEXT` | 0x03 | `A=nodeId, B=arenaRef` |
| `SET_DATE` | 0x04 (draft) | `A=nodeId, B=days since epoch (I32), C=millis of day (U32)` |

Value types (`constants.rs:187-196`): `U8=0x01, U32=0x02, I32=0x03, F32=0x04, STRING=0x05, ENUM=0x06, COLOR=0x07, DESIGN_TOKEN=0x08`.

### Component types (must map to native widgets) — `constants.rs:204-273`, `spec/PRIMITIVES.md`
| ID | Component | GTK mapping (reference) |
|---|---|---|
| 0x01 | TEXT | GtkLabel |
| 0x02 | IMAGE | GtkPicture |
| 0x03 | COLOR | GtkDrawingArea (fill) |
| 0x04 | SHAPE | GtkDrawingArea (`SHAPE_KIND`) |
| 0x05 | DIVIDER | GtkSeparator |
| 0x06 | SPACER | expanding box |
| 0x07 | PROGRESS_VIEW | GtkProgressBar / GtkSpinner |
| 0x08 | GAUGE | GtkLevelBar |
| 0x10/0x11 | VSTACK/HSTACK | GtkBox (orientation) |
| 0x12 | ZSTACK | GtkOverlay |
| 0x13/0x15/0x16 | GRID/LAZY_VGRID/LAZY_HGRID | GtkGrid |
| 0x14 | SCROLLVIEW | GtkScrolledWindow |
| 0x1B/0x1C | LAZY_VSTACK/LAZY_HSTACK | GtkBox (eager) |
| 0x20 | BUTTON | GtkButton |
| 0x21 | TEXT_FIELD | GtkEntry |

### EVENT commands the renderer **emits** (host → guest) — `constants.rs:54-91`, `spec/EVENTS.md`
`POINTER_DOWN=0x01`, `POINTER_MOVE=0x02` (flags `HOVER_ENTER=0x0001`/`HOVER_LEAVE=0x0002`), `POINTER_UP=0x03` (flag `POINTER_SECONDARY=0x0001`), `KEY_DOWN=0x04`/`KEY_UP=0x05` (modifiers u8: Shift=1, Ctrl=2, Alt=4, Meta=8; `KEY_REPEAT=0x0002`), `VALUE_CHANGED=0x06`, `TEXT_CHANGED=0x07` (string via event arena/batch string section), `FOCUS_CHANGED=0x08`, `EDITING_CHANGED=0x09`, `SUBMIT=0x0A`, `SCROLL=0x0B`, `WHEEL=0x0C`, `DATE_CHANGED=0x0D`, `NAVIGATE=0x0E` (global, `A=0`, flag `NAVIGATE_URL=0x0001`; no flag = back request).

Typed `Event` enum + encode/decode: `lib/rust/crates/pathland-core/src/events.rs:26-105` (encode :115-267; `decode_event` with event-arena string resolution :386-404). Event guards are **MANDATORY** (`spec/EVENTS.md:46-62`): an interaction is only emitted if the node has the matching `EVENT_LISTENERS` bit, is a value-bearing control, or carries `ACTION_ID`/`BINDING_ID`. The GTK renderer implements this in `desired_listeners` (`lib.rs:1137-1146`) and `attach_control_events` gated by `BINDING_ID` (`lib.rs:404-462`).

### META commands (`constants.rs:94-104`)
`RESET=0x01` (clear all output; also resets the event-arena cursor — `lib.rs:569-578` in core), `ENVIRONMENT=0x02` (fields `VIEWPORT_WIDTH=0x0001`, `VIEWPORT_HEIGHT=0x0002`, `ROUTE=0x0003`), `RESYNC=0x03` (host → guest request for full snapshot). **The GTK renderer currently ignores META** (its `apply_frame` match in `host.rs:175-267` has no META arm) — a Qt renderer should handle at least `RESET` (clear its id→widget map) and `RESYNC`.

## (c) Internal organization of the GTK renderer

**Files** (all under `lib/rust/crates/pathland-render-gtk/src/`):

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `lib.rs` (1951 lines) | `GtkRenderer` struct + widget build/update/reconcile, `WidgetKind`, `Pump` trait, `run`/`run_with_pump`/`run_with_pump_sized`, event controllers, CSS style application, tests |
| `host.rs` (568 lines) | `HostNode` + `RenderTree` — the retained decoded tree (the "native-element description"), `apply_frame` (TREE/STYLE opcode → tree delta), design-token resolution, `concrete_default_tables` |
| `layout.rs` (316 lines) | Pure display-free mapping: `stack_layout`, `align_from`, `padding_from`, `grid_columns`, `grid_cell_position` |
| `capi.rs` (145 lines) | C ABI (`pathland_gtk_run`, `pathland_gtk_run_ring`) + the two borrowed-handle `Pump` impls |
| `tokens.rs` (138 lines) | GTK-native token default enrichment (theme `@theme_*` colors via `StyleContext::lookup_color`), `scheme_from_settings` |

**Key types:**
- `GtkRenderer` (`lib.rs:70-97`): holds `tree: RenderTree`, `widgets: HashMap<u32, gtk::Widget>` (the id→widget map), `attached_listeners: HashMap<u32, u32>` (idempotency guard against double-attaching controllers), `composite_boxes`, `event_sink: Option<Rc<RefCell<dyn FnMut(Event)>>>`, `native_ctx: Option<gtk::StyleContext>`, plus `nav_views`/`nav_pages`/`nav_reconciling` for the `AdwNavigationView` adapter.
- `HostNode` (`host.rs:18-40`): `id`, `component_type`, `text`, `parent`, `children`, `properties: HashMap<u16,u32>` (numeric bits), `strings: HashMap<u16,String>` (STRING props resolved at apply time), `token_refs: BTreeMap<u16,String>`.
- `RenderTree` (`host.rs:85-101`): `nodes: HashMap<u32, HostNode>`, token override/default tables, `scheme`.

**Core flow:**
1. `apply_frame(frame)` (`lib.rs:159-162`) → `RenderTree::apply_frame` (decode delta) → `sync()`.
2. `sync()` (`lib.rs:172-195`): drop stale widgets; pre-order `sync_node` walk.
3. `sync_node(id)` (`lib.rs:197-222`): `get_or_create` → `update` (text/style/listeners/control events) → recurse children → `sync_container` (children reconciliation).
4. `get_or_create` (`lib.rs:251-271`): `build_widget(node)` (pure component→widget factory, `lib.rs:933-1019`), registers nav slots, captures the first style context to enrich token defaults.
5. `update` (`lib.rs:274-399`): `apply_padding` (margins), `apply_style` (visible/opacity/size/CSS), `attach_listeners` (pointer gestures + motion), `attach_control_events` (value/text changed), then per-`WidgetKind` property application.
6. Container reconciliation: `sync_stack_children` (`lib.rs:505-529`, re-appends tree-ordered children), `sync_grid_children` (`lib.rs:532-553`, row-major `GtkGrid::attach`), `sync_scroll_children` (`lib.rs:556-573`, single child), `sync_overlay_children` (`lib.rs:577-600`).
7. `run_with_pump_sized` (`lib.rs:1417-1547`): owns `gtk::Application`, builds the window, installs scheme detection + the window-level `EventControllerKey` for Escape/BackSpace → `Event::Navigate{url:None}`, sets the event sink, does initial render, then a `glib::idle_add_local` pump that calls `pump_once` (`lib.rs:1582-1596`) to drain pending frames. Re-entrant control events during frame apply are **deferred** to the idle pump (`pending` vec + `flush_pending`, `lib.rs:1474-1489, 1560-1578`) to avoid `RefCell` double-borrow panics.

**Event emission internals:** pointer down/up via `GestureClick` with `PropagationPhase::Capture` (`attach_pointer_gesture`, `lib.rs:1152-1184`), motion via `EventControllerMotion` (`attach_motion`, `lib.rs:1188-1221`). Buttons get `POINTER_DOWN|MOVE|UP` by default (`desired_listeners`, `lib.rs:1137-1146`); any node can add bits via `EVENT_LISTENERS`.

## (d) Qt-relevant observations

1. **The empty/foreign-argv pattern is critical and directly reusable.** GTK is given a bare program name rather than the host process's argv: `run_with_pump_sized("org.pathland.GtkDemo", ..., &["GtkDemo"], ...)` (`capi.rs:90-102, 132-144`). Rationale documented at `capi.rs:86-89` and `lib.rs:1399-1401`: the JVM's `-cp`/`-D` flags must never be parsed as GTK options, and an empty argv triggers a macOS activation quirk. A Qt renderer embedding inside a JVM/foreign host must do the same with `QApplication` args (Qt's `QApplication` also parses argv; `-XstartOnFirstThread` analog applies on macOS).

2. **Threading is strictly single-threaded on the toolkit main thread.** `pathland_gtk_run*` blocks until the GTK main loop exits; all `Pump` access happens on the GTK main thread (`capi.rs:31, 36-38, 55-57`). The host re-enters `pathland_native_*`/the ring **from the wake callback on the same thread**. A Qt renderer would follow the identical pattern (`QApplication::exec`, everything on the Qt main thread, host re-entry from the wake callback).

3. **Re-entrancy hazard is already solved in a toolkit-agnostic way.** Applying a frame that sets a control's value fires the native signal synchronously and re-enters `emit` while the pump is `RefCell`-borrowed → panic. The GTK renderer defers such events to an idle callback (`lib.rs:1466-1489, 1531-1542`, status.md:110-116). A Qt renderer must do the same (Qt signals are also synchronous — `QSlider::setValue` fires `valueChanged` synchronously).

4. **The renderer never drains events.** It only *writes* EVENT opcodes and wakes the host (`Pump` doc, `lib.rs:45-51`); the host drains via `RingTransport::drain_events` / `pathland_native_drain_events` / `pathland_core_drain_events`. Keep this contract.

5. **`widget_kind`/`build_widget`/`layout` are headless-testable pure functions.** Qt's equivalent (component→QWidget factory + layout mapping) can be tested the same way (the GTK crate proves widget *construction* headlessly, e.g. `renderer_placeholder_compiles` `lib.rs:1764-1767`).

6. **Design-token + scheme handling is renderer-owned.** A Qt renderer must provide Tier-1 light/dark default token tables (`host.rs:294-396`), accept `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` overrides, resolve `DESIGN_TOKEN`-typed properties at apply time (`RenderTree::resolve_tokens`, `host.rs:146-170`), and derive the scheme from the platform (`scheme_from_settings`, `tokens.rs:36-47`). GTK resolves tokens to *concrete* values because GTK CSS has no custom properties (status.md:89-90) — Qt style sheets have the same limitation, so the concrete-resolution path is the model.

7. **Navigation integration** (native `AdwNavigationView` adapter keyed by `ROUTE`+`NAV_DEPTH`+`NAV_CHROME`) is a significant chunk of the GTK renderer (`lib.rs:622-734, 826-869, 1242-1264`; status.md:50-68). A Qt equivalent would map onto `QStackedWidget`/`QStackView` — optional for a first Qt milestone, but the depth-reconcile logic (`nav_action`, `lib.rs:861-869`) is pure and directly portable.

8. **Gaps the GTK renderer documents** (status.md:118-134) apply equally to a Qt port: SHAPE Path approximation, MENU without a popover item list, no `ACTION_ID`-only gating, composite bodies only on button-like controls, lazy views render eagerly.

9. **Cargo dependencies** (`pathland-render-gtk/Cargo.toml:18-21`): `gtk4 = "0.9"`, `glib = "0.20"`, `pango = "0.20"`, `libadwaita = { version = "0.7", features = ["v1_4"] }`. The crate is `cdylib`+`rlib`. A Qt renderer crate would be structurally identical (cdylib + rlib, deps `qt_*`/`qt-wayland` crates or C++ shim), and must keep `pathland-core` + `pathland-view` `no_std` (checked by `lib/rust/check-wasm.sh`) — i.e. the renderer is the only desktop-only layer.

## (e) Test infrastructure used by renderers

- **Rust unit tests headless**: `cargo test -p pathland-render-gtk` — exercises `RenderTree` decode from real frames (built with `pathland_engine::Engine` + `pathland_view` DSL), delta frames, string property resolution, `widget_kind` full component map, container/composite kinds, nav-slot detection + `nav_action` + `NAV_CHROME`, stack layout mapping from hand-crafted opcode frames (`lib.rs:1858-1930`), and design-token resolution/overrides/scheme change (`lib.rs:1636-1761`). Widget construction is exercised **without a display** (`renderer_placeholder_compiles`, `lib.rs:1764-1767`).
- **Cargo.toml dev-dependencies** (`pathland-render-gtk/Cargo.toml:23-25`): `pathland-engine`, `pathland-view` — the renderer tests build trees with the DSL and emit into real ring memory.
- **HTML renderer**: `cargo test -p pathland-render-html` — 37 headless render tests (status.md:124-128); C ABI tests hand-craft `PLPL` batches with `encode_frame` and assert the returned C string (`capi.rs:73-162`).
- **C-ABI crates**: `cargo test -p pathland-core-capi` (ring push/read via raw `ring_ptr` header offsets, arena, event round-trip — `lib.rs:192-289`); `cargo test -p pathland-view-native` (flat-world emission, signal deltas — `lib.rs:362-384`; integration tests in `tests/native.rs`).
- **Golden conformance vectors**: `spec/CONFORMANCE.md` + `pathland-core/src/conformance.rs` pin exact byte layouts (e.g. `navigate_back_matches_conformance_vector_bytes`, `events.rs:547-554`).
- **Java side**: `mvn test -pl pathland-gtk-demo` — `RingEventReaderTest` (5 headless tests, no GTK); the wider Java reactor (`mvn install`) covers the emitter/wire codec. The `pathland-render-html` jar embeds the Rust cdylib (built by the Rust job) and `cargo build -p pathland-render-html` must run before `mvn test`.
- **Whole workspace**: `cd lib/rust && cargo test`; demo smoke runs via `scripts/run-rust-gtk-demo.sh` and `scripts/run-java-gtk-demo.sh` (the latter builds both dylibs, sets `-Dpathland.core.lib`/`-Dpathland.gtk.lib`, and passes `-XstartOnFirstThread` on macOS).
- **Guard scripts**: `lib/rust/check-wasm.sh` enforces `no_std` + `wasm32-unknown-unknown` on the protocol core (the Qt renderer, like GTK, lives outside that constraint).
